This establishes a uniform Markov property for these states. The authors build a classical representation using projective 2-designs, which yields a convergent cluster expansion with positive weights despite noncommutativity. entry.title: Quantum search for the minimum using numerical estimators with optimal query counts
entry.summary: Query-Optimal Quantum Minimum Finding from Numerical Estimators arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper proposes a quantum minimum-finding algorithm for objectives accessed through numerical estimators, avoiding the logarithmic overhead of amplifying estimate confidence before searching. At constant confidence, it finds a 2ε-optimal label using O(√N) base-estimator queries. The authors also give a result for preparations assigning known probability mass p to low objective values, with O(p^{-1/2}) queries. Applications include selecting near-optimal bounded expectations and guided ground-energy estimation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose quantum minimum finding avoiding logarithmic confidence amplification, claiming O(√N) queries and worst-case tight bounds for the additive error.

entry.title: Fast, in-place quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion that need no ancilla qubits
entry.summary: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents quantum algorithms that perform integer multiplication, modular multiplication modulo a power of two, and modular inversion in place, overwriting the input with the output. These operations use O(n^{1+ε}) gates for any ε>0, with no ancilla qubits in most cases and only logarithmically many for one variant. The authors state these are the first quantum algorithms to achieve both subquadratic gate counts and sublinear ancilla counts for each of these in-place operations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first in-place quantum multiplication and inversion with subquadratic gates and sublinear ancillas, unified under one theorem, mainly affecting quantum arithmetic theory.

entry.title: Stabilizing the Two-Photon Dicke Model Hamiltonian
entry.summary: Hamiltonian Stabilization of the Two-Photon Dicke Model arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies a model of N emitters coupled to light through collective two-photon interactions, which can make the energy spectrum unbounded and prevent a stable thermodynamic bright phase. The authors add a positive Kac-scaled number-Kerr interaction, which keeps the Hamiltonian bounded from below at all couplings while preserving its generalized Z4 symmetry. They derive the exact zero-temperature energy density and global phase diagram, and support the results with symmetry-resolved exact diagonalization up to N=128. ★★★★ Notable: The authors stabilize the two-photon Dicke model via a positive Kac-scaled Kerr term, giving an exact zero-temperature energy density and first-order phase diagram.

entry.title: Quantum error correction when noise is uneven and decoders have inaccurate information
entry.summary: When the Noise Gets Noisy: Quantum Error Correction with Disordered Noise and Misinformed Decoding arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies quantum error correction when noise varies across space and time and the decoder has incomplete or inaccurate knowledge of it, modeling physical error rates as random variables. The authors show that decoding performance is governed by the entropy and Bhattacharyya coefficients of the noise distribution. Numerical tests on surface codes agree with the theory across several noise settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model physical error rates as random variables, characterizing decoding performance via entropy and Bhattacharyya coefficients, with surface-code simulations reported to agree with theory.

entry.title: Joining quantum codes into quilts for logic without extra ancilla qubits
entry.summary: Stitching Quantum Codes into Quilts: Universal Logic with no Ancillary Qubits arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper introduces the "code quilt," a construction that directly measures a joint logical operator across two or more codeblocks without an ancillary system. The authors give explicit measurement circuits that need no physical qubits beyond those already used for idle syndrome extraction. The construction is based on a subsystem code, and several sufficient conditions are given under which code-capacity distance is preserved. Empirical analysis on bivariate bicycle and surface codes is reported, including decoding experiments comparing logical error rates to idle memory. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a code quilt construction measuring multi-codeblock logical operators without ancillas; the abstract reports experiments on bivariate bicycle and surface codes with decoding resu

entry.title: Non-contextual Pauli Hamiltonians are free fermions in disguise
entry.summary: All Non-Contextual Pauli Hamiltonians are Free-Fermion in Disguise arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how to split quantum Hamiltonians into fragments that classical computers can handle, using non-contextual sets of Pauli operators. It shows that non-contextual Pauli Hamiltonians are free fermions in disguise and can be written with Majorana and Dirac fermion operators in a Jordan–Wigner-like encoding. Both central theorems are formalized in the Lean proof assistant. The authors also propose a heuristic algorithm for finding line-graph-based free-fermion fragments in molecular Hamiltonians. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show non-contextual Pauli Hamiltonians are free-fermion-disguised, give a Jordan-Wigner-like encoding, formalize theorems in Lean, and benchmark on molecular Hamiltonians.

entry.title: A new polynomial-style method for lower bounds on DQC1 query complexity
entry.summary: A sensitivity-constrained polynomial method for DQC1 query complexity arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces a polynomial-style technique for proving lower bounds in the DQC1 quantum query model, based on a measure called sensitivity approximate degree for Boolean functions. It shows that every nonconstant total Boolean function on N inputs requires Ω(N) queries in DQC1, so DQC1 gives no asymptotic speedup for such functions. For symmetric partial functions, the paper characterizes this measure and derives tight quadratic separations from BQP query complexity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce sensitivity approximate degree for DQC1 queries, report Ω(N) lower bounds for total functions, and tight quadratic separations from BQP.

entry.title: Classical complexity of quantum state transmission: the minimum classical communication cost of sending quantum states
entry.summary: The classical complexity of quantum state transmission arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper asks how hard it is to transmit quantum information using only classical communication. It defines classical communication models for quantum preparations and their minimum cost, called classical complexity. The authors prove this cost equals the classical communication needed to simulate quantum correlations in prepare-and-broadcast experiments, establishing a resource equivalence. They also characterise the classical complexity of noisy quantum states and present methods to certify it in quantum preparation devices. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define classical complexity of quantum state transmission, prove a resource equivalence with quantum correlations, and report exponential growth with quantum dimension.

entry.title: Precise experiment on s-polarized evanescent-wave reflection and the Casimir puzzle
entry.summary: Precise experimental investigation of the reflection properties caused by s-polarized evanescent waves and the Casimir puzzle arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The authors measured the amplitude and phase of low-frequency magnetic fields reflected from a metal plate, produced by an oscillating magnetic dipole. These quantities are determined entirely by transverse electric (s) polarized evanescent waves. The data disagree quantitatively and qualitatively with predictions using the standard Drude response function, which the authors say is excluded in this low-frequency region. The results are presented as clarifying causes of the Casimir puzzle. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors directly measure reflected low-frequency s-polarized evanescent magnetic fields and report that the Drude response is excluded, bearing on the Casimir puzzle.

entry.title: Entanglement-assisted quantum differential privacy: a framework against entanglement attacks
entry.summary: Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Differential Privacy arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper identifies an entanglement attack, in which an adversary sends one half of an entangled state to a quantum computer running a privacy mechanism, keeps the other half, and measures both jointly. The authors show this attack can fully break a mechanism that has a finite quantum differential privacy parameter. They propose entanglement-assisted quantum differential privacy (EA-QDP), characterize when a mechanism has a finite parameter, and show the optimal parameter can be computed by semidefinite programming. The depolarizing channel is recommended for bounding the extra leakage, and experiments on simulated and physical quantum hardware agree with the theory. ★★★★ Notable: The authors identify an entanglement attack, define EA-QDP, compute optimal parameters via SDP, and report validation on simulated and physical hardware.

entry.title: Algorithmic quantum sensing: using classical and quantum algorithms to measure time-varying fields
entry.summary: Algorithmic Quantum Sensing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a unified framework for measuring time-dependent fields using classical and quantum algorithms. It introduces three pulse-sequence protocols and quantum computational spectroscopy (QCS), which links quantum sensors to a quantum processor. The authors report that QCS surpasses the Heisenberg limit and keeps this advantage under certain noise conditions. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce quantum computational spectroscopy, reporting polynomial gains beyond the Heisenberg limit, with proofs of a fundamental separation from non-quantum-computational protocols.

entry.title: An end-to-end quantum algorithm for solving a biomolecular simulation equation
entry.summary: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents an end-to-end quantum algorithm that takes classical inputs and returns classical outputs, targeting the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann (LPB) equation, a partial differential equation with variable coefficients used to simulate biomolecular systems. The authors implement every step, including state preparation, generating the quantum solution, and estimating system properties, and introduce a discrete representation for variable-coefficient PDEs on a grid. They report that the required circuit size scales polylogarithmically in the number of grid points and in the inverse accuracy, giving an exponential improvement in grid-point scaling over classical methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present an end-to-end quantum algorithm with a new discrete operator representation for variable-coefficient PDEs, reporting polylogarithmic scaling in grid size.

entry.title: Scaling classical hardware to make real-time quantum error correction both fast and accurate
entry.summary: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper introduces Rapids, a streaming neural decoder co-designed with a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) to be both fast and accurate for quantum error correction. For the distance-19 surface code, it decodes each syndrome round in under a microsecond on a single FPGA. Its logical error rate is 240 times lower than existing real-time hardware decoders. The authors also show the design extends to other codes and scales across multiple FPGAs or custom silicon. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors co-design a neural decoder with an FPGA, reporting sub-microsecond decoding for the distance-19 surface code with a 240x lower logical error rate than existing real-time decoders.

entry.title: Classical algorithm for estimating ground energy of certain interacting fermion systems
entry.summary: Efficient Classical Algorithms for Ground Energy Estimation of Fermions with Conjugate-Pair Orbital Interactions arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents an efficient classical randomized algorithm for approximating the ground energy of fermionic Hamiltonians with conjugate hopping matrices and conjugate-paired orbital interactions, including attractive Hubbard models. The guarantee holds without assuming a physical spectral gap or weak coupling, and covers interactions beyond onsite density attractions. The method reduces ground-energy estimation to partition-function estimation, uses a discretization with controlled energy error to obtain a nonnegative weighted sum of squared determinant moduli, and applies the Chen–Liu log-concave counting theorem. The authors also obtain a sharper arithmetic bound by controlling the number of sampling runs and matrix updates and by using sparse matrices to reduce per-update cost. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce fermionic ground-energy estimation to partition-function estimation and apply the Chen–Liu log-concave counting theorem, reporting polynomial-time classical randomized guarantees fo

entry.title: Computational complexity of bosonic Lindbladian fixed points
entry.summary: The computational complexity of bosonic Lindbladian fixed points arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how hard it is to estimate observables and sample from stationary states (fixed points) of bosonic Lindbladian dynamics, which describe open quantum systems. It maps out a broad complexity landscape, covering universal quantum computation, efficient classical simulation, sampling hardness, and undecidability. The authors also show that deciding whether a stationary density operator exists is RE-hard, even for purely dissipative Lindbladians. ★★★★ Notable: The authors map the complexity of bosonic Lindbladian fixed points, reporting universal quantum computation embeddings, sampling hardness results, and RE-hardness, with proofs and tight bounds.

entry.title: Measuring local velocity in atomic superfluids, from Riemann waves to quantized vortices
entry.summary: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents a method for measuring local velocity in two-dimensional atomic superfluids. It uses matter-wave interferometry based on Raman-Bragg beam splitters to map the local gradient of the superfluid's wavefunction phase onto shifts of interference fringes, reconstructing the 2D velocity field. The technique is applied to two canonical problems: directly observing the self-similar evolution of velocity in 1D Riemann rarefaction flows, and mapping the full 2D velocity field around quantized vortices, demonstrating quantized velocity circulation.

entry.title: Simulating strongly correlated electrons on large lattices with neural Gaussian tensor networks
entry.summary: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper introduces neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which use the locally entangled subspace of Gaussian states to fit better with modern neural networks. The method has an exact contraction cost of O(N^{3/2}) on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at U/t=8 and 1/8 hole doping, it yields state-of-the-art variational energies on lattices of up to 1024 sites.

entry.title: Highly Accurate Neural-Network Quantum States Using Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
entry.summary: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics arXiv · Nov 20, 2026Neural-network quantum states are used to approximate ground states, but their non-energy observables converge more slowly than energy does. This paper introduces dynamical averaging, which estimates expectation values by averaging a state or observable evolved in real time. The authors prove that errors in arbitrary ground-state observables can be suppressed up to quadratically, matching energy's convergence rate. Tests on non-integrable spin models show faster convergence and substantially smaller observable errors.

entry.title: Training quantum samplers classically, with shared learning and fine-tuning for quantum matter
entry.summary: Classically Trained Quantum Generative Models with Shared Training and Fine Tuning for Quantum Matter arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper trains a hypernetwork that maps Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles, sharing information across a phase diagram before local fine-tuning with reference data. It derives an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator for Fourier coefficients of Pauli-rotation circuits and introduces a CDF-KL loss for comparing selected marginals. The method is studied on the Haldane Hamiltonian and the transverse-field Ising model, with results compared against independently trained circuits.

entry.title: Authenticating quantum key distribution with random position checks
entry.summary: Authenticating quantum key distribution through random position checks arXiv · Nov 20, 2026Quantum key distribution needs authentication so that parties do not unknowingly share a key with an impersonator. This paper proposes a protocol that uses one party's position as the authentication credential. It is built on BB84 with quantum position verification rounds randomly interleaved. The authors give an initial security analysis for a restricted set of attacks.

entry.title: A paper on designing sequential quantum repeaters that use error detection
entry.summary: On the design of sequential quantum repeaters with error detection arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how to design sequential quantum repeater schemes for long-distance quantum communication over a repeater chain, using quantum key distribution as a benchmark. It finds that simple quantum error-detecting codes, such as repetition codes or quantum parity codes, perform well under near-term hardware assumptions and outperform schemes without encoding. The authors also compare different architectures for generating initial entanglement and show that moderate hardware improvements can partly offset slow progress in other components.

entry.title: Imaginary-time density correlations encode quantum entropy and free energy
entry.summary: Imaginary-Time Density Correlations Encode Quantum Entropy and Free Energy arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper notes that a classical maximum-entropy estimate of excess entropy from the static structure factor fails for quantum systems. The authors show that imaginary-time density correlations contain the missing information and derive closed-form expressions for excess entropy and free energies via relative-entropy inference with an ideal Bose or Fermi gas as reference. The formulas can be evaluated from path-integral simulations or X-ray Thomson scattering data and are tested on weakly interacting bosons, interacting fermions on a ring, and the warm dense electron gas.

entry.title: How unequal coupling strengths affect two atoms decaying and becoming entangled in one shared cavity
entry.summary: Effect of coupling asymmetry on the spontaneous decay and entanglement of two atoms in a common cavity arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper studies how two identical two-level atoms spontaneously decay into vacuum inside a cavity at low temperature. By calculating the exact self-energy with both atoms initially excited, the authors analytically derive the system's survival probability and state amplitudes. They find that moderate coupling asymmetry speeds up the decay of the survival probability and increases entanglement production in both lossless and lossy cavities.

entry.title: Quantum Zeno effect when measurement timing is in superposition
entry.summary: Quantum Zeno Effect with a Superposed Measurement Schedule in Relational Time arXiv · Nov 20, 2026Inspired by the Page-Wootters construction, in which time is a quantum clock reading, this paper proposes a quantum circuit that treats measurement timing as a quantum degree of freedom. A schedule qubit places two Zeno measurement schedules of a driven qubit in coherent superposition. The authors report that the interference visibility between the schedules depends only on their time offset, and they give a superconducting-qubit circuit with gate count and error budget.

entry.title: Entanglement, readable records, and quantum recovery in qubit chains
entry.summary: Entanglement, records, and quantum recovery in qubit chains arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies entanglement, readable records, and quantum recovery using an exactly solvable chain of sequentially interacting qubits. For weak interactions, entanglement reaches a later environment site before that site carries an equally strong local record. It also examines how accessible the relative phase is and derives the optimal fidelity for recovering an unknown quantum state from the system and an accessible environment fragment.

entry.title: Quantum autoencoder on real hardware for spotting new physics at muon colliders
entry.summary: Quantum Autoencoder on Real Hardware for New Physics Searches at Muon Colliders arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper applies a quantum autoencoder to search for new physics in the tri-photon process at muon colliders. Using a six-qubit circuit on the Tianyan176 quantum computer, the authors measure reconstruction losses for Standard Model events and anomalous quartic gauge coupling events. The hardware-implemented autoencoder effectively separates new-physics signals from the Standard Model background. The paper also derives expected constraints on the anomalous quartic gauge coupling coefficients and compares them with conventional methods.

entry.title: Measuring how non-realistic quantum random access codes must be
entry.summary: Quantifying the irrealism required by quantum random access codes arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper asks how far decoding observables must depart from having elements of reality to achieve a given quantum advantage in a communication task, focusing on quantum random access codes. Irrealism is defined as the relative entropy to the closest state where the unrevealed measurement leaves the preparation undisturbed, and it applies to both prepare-and-measure and entanglement-assisted codes. The authors derive the exact irrealism frontier for prepare-and-measure codes decoded in mutually unbiased bases, and analyze the required irrealism and its link to nonlocality for entanglement-assisted codes.

entry.title: Fast extraction of universal data from temporal spectra, applied to Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering
entry.summary: Fast extraction of universal data from temporal spectrum: Applications to Haagerup CFT and monopole scattering arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper proposes a fast algorithm that reads a conformal field theory (CFT) spectrum from the transfer matrix spectrum of an infinite matrix product state after a short imaginary-time evolution. The authors use it to obtain the charge-resolved spectrum of a Haagerup CFT to higher levels, yielding a central charge c = 2.137(27). They also show that the Maldacena–Ludwig monopole boundary can be realized as the ground state of the Fidkowski–Kitaev Hamiltonian after a space-time rotation.

entry.title: A faster way to calculate the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled photon pairs
entry.summary: Efficient calculation of the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled biphotons arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies the spatial biphoton state produced by spontaneous parametric down-conversion, a state useful for high-dimensional quantum information processing. The authors present a generating-function method that analytically performs the four-dimensional transverse spatial integral without approximating the phase-matching function. The source geometry is described by a few dimensionless parameters, enabling efficient and numerically stable calculation at high mode orders.

entry.title: Tracking time-varying quantum Hamiltonians with adaptive quantum reinforcement learning
entry.summary: Adaptive Hamiltonian Identification via Quantum Reinforcement Learning under Non-Stationary Dynamics arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper treats identifying the Hamiltonian that governs a quantum system as a quantum reinforcement learning problem, where a quantum agent processes sequential state observations to estimate parameters. A Vanilla-QRL agent handles stationary dynamics, and a recurrent GRU-QRL architecture is introduced to track non-stationary dynamics. Tests on transverse-field Ising models cover abrupt switching, rapid changes, and gradual drift, with comparison to a QGRNN baseline. Both methods reconstruct stationary Hamiltonians accurately, while GRU-QRL tracks non-stationary dynamics substantially better.

entry.title: Whether dephasing helps or hurts a simulated quantum reservoir's learning, depending on the task
entry.summary: To predict or to persist: how decoherence shapes learning in a spin-qubit quantum reservoir arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper simulates a six-qubit spin chain with Markovian dissipation to study how dephasing and the choice of measured observables affect learning. Combining single- and two-qubit observables gives better predictions than a population-only readout at comparable polynomial feature counts. For chaotic forecasting at T2=1 μs, prediction horizons shorten in all 10 reservoir realizations relative to a reference with relaxation and dephasing disabled. The authors conclude that the impact of coherence depends strongly on the task.

entry.title: Single-photon emission boosted by cooperative effects in a topological emitter chain
entry.summary: Cooperativity-enhanced single-photon emission in a topological quantum emitter chain arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes using cooperative effects in a topological single-photon emitter chain to tailor single-photon emission. It shows that multiple emitters normally suppress single-photon emission, but localized topological edge modes restore it and protect against local perturbations. The collective nature of these edge modes also produces directional emission and linewidth narrowing.

entry.title: Boosting signal-to-noise ratio by postselecting coincident photon detections for quantum key distribution and anticounterfeiting
entry.summary: Improving the signal-to-noise ratio through postselection of coincident detections in anticounterfeiting and quantum key distribution arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a simple method for weak optical signals carried by simultaneously emitted photon pairs or multiplets. Keeping only coincident detections on two detectors improves the signal-to-noise ratio, sometimes greatly. Genuine coincidences stay roughly constant while the postselection window remains wide enough, whereas accidental coincidences drop linearly as the window narrows. The authors analyze applications to quantum key distribution, metrology, and anticounterfeiting.

entry.title: Role of complementarity and quantum correlation in uncertainty relations and optimal states
entry.summary: The role of complementarity and quantum correlation in the uncertainty relations and the optimum states arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines uncertainty relations in quantum mechanics, which set a lower bound on the product of two observables' dispersions depending on their first-order quantum correlation and commutation relation. The authors show that the complex parameter in the optimum state equation has real and imaginary parts that depend on the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation, respectively. Applied to a two-level system, they find these two quantities complement each other for two spin-1/2 projections in the optimum state.

entry.title: Ellis: A Very Fast Simulator for Quantum Circuits Under Qubit Loss and Leakage
entry.summary: Ellis: Extremely Fast Quantum Circuit Simulation under Qubit Loss and Leakage arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper presents Ellis, a method and open-source tool for simulating quantum circuits affected by qubit loss and leakage. The authors show that several key fault-tolerant primitives keep a common reference measurement record under loss, allowing exact Pauli-frame simulation with per-shot masks. They also provide a near-linear-time procedure to certify whether a circuit has this property. On the gross code, the authors report 952,000 shots per second on one CPU core, at least 1000 times faster than Clifft and PPVM.

entry.title: A receiver-side method to verify phase randomization in time-bin BB84 quantum key distribution with weak coherent pulses
entry.summary: A receiver-side approach to confirm phase randomization in BB84 time-bin QKD with weak coherent pulses arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses time-bin BB84 quantum key distribution, which uses weak coherent pulses and requires random relative phases between symbol pulses. Phase randomization is usually checked only on the sender's side. The authors propose a protocol that lets the receiver monitor and confirm phase randomization during operation. The method works at the single-photon level and needs no physical changes to the receiver, offering an extra way to detect eavesdropping that affects phase randomization.

entry.title: Local-channel inequivalence in analytic symmetry-broken phases
entry.summary: Local-channel inequivalence within analytic symmetry-broken phases arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper shows that Gibbs states at different temperatures can be inequivalent under two-way quasi-local channels even within one phase with spontaneously broken continuous symmetry and analytic free energy. The systems studied are a canonical ideal Bose gas and a classical vortex-free Villain model on hypercubic lattices. At lower temperatures, distant observers can estimate the shared order direction more accurately, with maximal mutual information growing logarithmically in region radius and a constant term that is strictly larger at lower temperatures.

entry.title: Bose-Einstein condensation driven far from equilibrium
entry.summary: Genuinely Out-of-Equilibrium Bose-Einstein Condensation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Bose-Einstein condensation usually occurs in the ground state, but excitons have a vacuum ground state and therefore condense only under out-of-equilibrium conditions that counter rapid decay. The paper develops a driven-dissipative framework showing that condensates form in one and two dimensions under sufficiently strong excitation. In three dimensions, including effective loss rates and a specified injection energy yields a percent-level condensate fraction, consistent in order of magnitude with the 2022 exciton experiment by Morita et al.

entry.title: Finite-key analysis of multi-antenna continuous-variable quantum key distribution
entry.summary: Finite-Key Analysis for Multiple-Antenna Quantum Key Distribution with Continuous Variables arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies applying multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) techniques to continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) with a finite number of exchanged signals. The authors show how data from the brief passes of low-earth-orbit satellites over ground stations can be used to estimate MIMO channel parameters, extract a secret key, and quantify the key generation rate. For a 2×2 MIMO setup with Gaussian encoding and heterodyne detection, the finite-key analysis indicates MIMO CV-QKD could outperform multiplexed and single-mode schemes. The authors also conjecture that the ultimate enhancement of a multi-antenna CV-QKD system is characterized by the product of its numbers of inputs and outputs.

entry.title: How quantum scarring affects the onset of chaos in Bohmian trajectories
entry.summary: The influence of quantum scarring on the onset of Bohmian chaos arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how stable and unstable periodic orbits of a perturbed two-dimensional oscillator shape the Bohmian trajectories of the corresponding quantum system. The authors find that all Bohmian trajectories in the studied systems become chaotic over long times and measure how long they take to reach an ergodic pattern. Trajectories near unstable periodic orbits reach this pattern systematically faster than those near stable orbits of the same period, a behaviour linked to scarring effects from both orbit types. The paper also examines how the Bohmian dynamics changes when a stable periodic orbit undergoes a bifurcation and becomes unstable.

entry.title: Flat bands and bound states in the continuum in non-Hermitian pseudospin lattices
entry.summary: Flat bands and bound states in the continuum in non-Hermitian pseudospin lattices arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies a class of one-dimensional non-Hermitian lattices whose Bloch Hamiltonians take a pseudospin form. For integer pseudospin, the system intrinsically has a zero-energy flat band and its compact localized states. Increasing non-Hermiticity pushes the dispersive bands toward the flat band so they overlap spectrally, turning those localized states into bound states in the continuum.

entry.title: A new quantum algorithm framework for estimating integer-order entropy
entry.summary: A New Quantum Algorithm Framework for Integer Order Entropy Estimation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a quantum algorithm framework for estimating Rényi entropy of a distribution at a fixed integer order. Given purified quantum query access, the algorithm estimates the entropy within a specified additive error and gives an upper bound on the number of queries. Its main technique is a recursive construction of collision states that retains and reuses intermediate states, combined with decreasing probability thresholds.

entry.title: A quantum genetic algorithm using entangled three-level qutrits to optimize benchmark test functions
entry.summary: A Quantum Genetic Algorithm for Optimization of Benchmark Test Functions using Entangled Qutrits arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies optimization of the Rastrigin, Rosenbrock, and Table Holder benchmark functions. It compares a classical genetic algorithm with a quantum genetic algorithm based on qubits and a higher-order version based on entangled qutrits, which are three-level quantum systems. The authors report that the quantum algorithm converges faster than the classical one and that solution quality is considerably improved.

entry.title: High-fidelity control of long-lived qubits using a noisy mediator qubit
entry.summary: High-fidelity control of long-lived data qubits via a noisy mediator arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a reset-assisted control method for manipulating long-lived data qubits that are difficult to control directly. Because mediator qubits have shorter coherence times, their relaxation and dephasing normally limit gate fidelity, and the method suppresses these errors through repeated mediator reinitialization. It achieves high-fidelity single- and two-qubit gates. An analytical quantum-trajectory analysis explains the mechanism and provides compact fidelity formulas.

entry.title: How nonmagnetic impurities affect Majorana braiding gates in vortex cores
entry.summary: Nonmagnetic Impurity Effects on Majorana Braiding Quantum Gates in Vortex Cores arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper uses time-dependent many-body simulations to study how nonmagnetic impurities affect braiding of Majorana zero modes in vortex cores. In the two-mode square-root-Z gate, sufficiently strong attractive impurities suppress the topological gap and reduce adiabaticity, degrading quantization of the geometric-phase difference, while the repulsive impurities considered cause no comparable damage. In the four-mode configuration, attractive impurities leave the low-energy spectrum nearly unchanged, whereas repulsive ones mainly suppress the first excited state. Slower braiding substantially raises the X gate success probability.

entry.title: Moiré-based recursive phase unwrapping for differential atom interferometry
entry.summary: Moiré-Enabled Recursive Phase Unwrapping for Differential Atom Interferometry arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a Moiré-enabled recursive phase unwrapping (MRPU) method for differential measurements with dual-species atom interferometers, aiming to reject vibration noise and determine relative acceleration. The authors emulated different atomic species using a rubidium-85 D1/D2 dual-scale-factor interferometer and achieved phase unwrapping over 5000 consecutive measurements under 40 rad equivalent vibrational noise. The relative-acceleration Allan deviation was 1.47×10^-8 g at 997 shots, and simulations showed a 9.76 to 26.03 dB increase in tolerable narrowband vibration amplitude.

entry.title: A method for designing low-error circuits that extract error syndromes in quantum codes
entry.summary: Structure-Guided Synthesis of Low-Error Syndrome Extraction Circuits arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how the order of gates in syndrome-extraction circuits affects error rates in quantum error correction, even when the ideal stabilizer measurements are the same. The authors propose a synthesis method for structured CSS codes that groups checks with recurring connectivity and shares one relative gate order per group, then uses a CP-SAT solver to set the shared orders and gate timings. The final circuit is chosen using noisy circuit simulations with decoding. Across 15 quantum LDPC codes from ten families, the method reports the lowest logical error rate estimates among the compared approaches.

entry.title: Critical droplets and metastability in long-range chains
entry.summary: Critical droplets and metastability in long-range chains arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how metastable states decay in one-dimensional Ising chains with long-range interactions, where decay proceeds through nucleation of critical droplets. For interactions decaying as 1/r^(1+σ), the droplet's surface cost depends on its size and competes with the bulk free-energy gain. The critical radius scales as h^(-1/σ) at small bias field h, and the activation barrier behaves differently for σ below, at, or above 1. A nonlocal φ^4 field theory and stochastic dynamics support these predicted scalings.

entry.title: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion computing
entry.summary: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a scheme for performing a transversal controlled-Z gate, applying entangling operations to multiple neighboring ion pairs simultaneously across double-well trapped-ion architectures. A tailored dynamical decoupling method suppresses unwanted couplings, and the authors analyze decoherence and crosstalk caused by laser wave-vector misalignment. They also examine how crosstalk-induced gate errors affect the fault-tolerant preparation of a logical Bell state between two [[4,1,2]] error-detection code blocks.

entry.title: Simulating insurance portfolio losses with a quantum circuit
entry.summary: Insurance portfolio simulation with a quantum circuit arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a Quantum Circuit Born Machine approach for modelling the joint loss distribution of an insurance portfolio. It combines a tail-focused discretisation of heavy-tailed marginals, a Monte Carlo-style training objective, and a two-stage scheme that trains on a simulator and fine-tunes on quantum hardware. On a mixed portfolio of equity returns and insurance losses, the trained circuit recovers the qualitative dependence structure.

entry.title: Linking entanglement and complexity via spacetime density matrices
entry.summary: Two Faces of Spacetime Density Matrices: Entanglement and Complexity arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper connects entanglement and complexity using spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench, which defines a state spread complexity called Krylov-Rényi complexity. The authors also construct Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe limit from first-order replica data.

entry.title: Calibrating Qubits During Error Correction by Amplifying Gate Errors
entry.summary: Syndrome-based Calibration Using Gate-Error Amplification arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents GEARS, a runtime calibration framework that tunes control parameters during quantum error correction using syndrome data and gate-error amplification. It repeats selected CZ gates and probes their controls in spatially separated groups to strengthen local calibration signals. Surface code simulations show that depth-three amplification reduces required measurements by about a factor of eight at matched gradient SNR and fixed probe strength, and cuts excess expected logical failures by roughly 31-40% in closed-loop calibration.

entry.title: Momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo study of twisted bilayer graphene including remote bands
entry.summary: Momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo for twisted bilayer graphene: Interaction effects in the presence of remote bands arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies strong correlation effects in twisted bilayer graphene by comparing a model projected onto the central flat bands with calculations that explicitly include remote bands. The authors extend momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo to incorporate the remote bands. They find the projected description remains reliable over a broad parameter range, while near the band-touching limit remote-band electrons acquire substantial low-energy spectral weight.

entry.title: Remote Use of Quantum Machines Under Adversarial Conditions
entry.summary: Remote Use of Quantum Machines in the Adversarial Scenario arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies the security problem of remotely operating quantum machines, where classical commands alone cannot ensure that only the intended user can prepare the inputs that activate the device. The authors model a competition between a remote user, Alice, and an adversary, Eve, who both hold correlations with the machine within quantum resource theory. For tasks with convex figures of merit, the competition is governed by complementary upper roofs, and for spectral tasks by an entanglement imbalance. The paper also orders the programming powers of Alice and Eve with a task-independent simulation preorder, concluding that shared quantum correlations are a key resource for controlling access to remote quantum machines.

entry.title: When Lies Look Like Noise: Certifying Untrusted Entanglement Swapping
entry.summary: When lies look like noise: certifying untrusted entanglement swapping arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper studies the security of entanglement swapping in quantum repeater networks, where intermediate nodes may misreport the classical outcome. It proposes a cut-and-choose protocol that tests a random subset of entangled pairs to certify the rest, with a finite-size guarantee. The authors also estimate the number of test pairs and the memory required for different misreport rates.

entry.title: Non-Binary Detector Error Models: A Noise Description Method for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Error Correction
entry.summary: Non-Binary Detector Error Models arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces non-binary detector error models (DEMs), in which each fault location of a syndrome extraction circuit is represented by one random variable over its original alphabet, such as the 16 two-qubit Pauli errors after a CNOT gate. The authors also propose a split-merge-regroup transformation that builds a compact non-binary DEM from any Clifford circuit. Numerical results on surface, color, and bivariate bicycle codes show that non-binary DEMs have four to five times fewer Tanner graph edges and perform better under belief propagation, with and without OSD post-processing, with BP plus OSD running up to 9.4 times faster on a CPU.

entry.title: A proof that certain high-dimensional photonic GHZ states cannot be built, found with AI
entry.summary: A Tensor-Algebraic No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional Photonic Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger States Discovered with AlphaProof Nexus arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper describes photonic GHZ states from probabilistic pair sources as complex-weighted, edge-coloured graphs. It proves that for even N ≥ 4 and D ≥ N, no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists, so such graphs cannot generate the N-photon D-dimensional GHZ state. The proof was discovered through AI-assisted formal proof search in Lean using AlphaProof Nexus.

entry.title: CAVQS: Context-aware variational quantum circuit synthesis using unitary redistribution and dynamic reconstruction
entry.summary: CAVQS: Context-Aware Variational Quantum Circuit Synthesis via Unitary Redistribution and Dynamic Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents CAVQS, a framework for variational quantum circuit synthesis that aims to reduce costly two-qubit gates. It uses QR decomposition to move unitary factors between overlapping blocks, enabling reductions across block boundaries, and builds ancilla-free dynamic implementations for blocks preceding permitted terminal measurements. On random-circuit targets, mean two-qubit gate counts fall by 28.79%-42.52% versus QFAST, 2.05%-52.62% versus SQUANDER, and 30.51%-74.64% versus Fast-USYN. On 4-6 qubit quantum algorithm benchmarks, the reductions are 27.27%-36.77%, 20.65%-69.10%, and 36.31%-71.88%, respectively.

entry.title: Evolved Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
entry.summary: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Quantum computers must continuously measure noisy quantum states, and a classical decoder must infer corrections fast enough to keep pace. The paper rewrites several published belief-propagation (BP) decoders for quantum LDPC codes in a domain-specific language and searches that language with grammatical evolution. The authors report that re-parameterized BP+OSD and BP+LSD decoders run much faster, and that evolved decoders achieve better trade-offs between decoding time and logical error rate. The evolved decoders are said to generalize well across noise levels, code sizes and round counts.

entry.title: Using boosting to learn from noisy quantum circuits, beyond error mitigation
entry.summary: Beyond Error Mitigation: Using Boosting for Noisy Quantum Machine Learning arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper compares boosting of noisy parameterized quantum circuits with probabilistic error cancellation for supervised binary classification. Under Pauli noise, the authors establish a common hypothesis-class complexity bound for both methods. In finite-shot teacher-student simulations with AdaBoostR and Real AdaBoost, boosting required fewer circuit executions to reach the same accuracy target as circuit depth and noise increased, and achieved higher test accuracy.

entry.title: Hybrid PointNet-quantum network with QFT variants for LiDAR point-cloud classification
entry.summary: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a hybrid PointNet-quantum neural network for classifying LiDAR point clouds, combining classical feature extraction, amplitude encoding, and a variational quantum circuit. Five Fourier-processing configurations are compared on KITTI, nuScenes, and PandaSet under ideal simulation and the IBM FakeManilaV2 noise model. Under ideal simulation, IQFT-After achieves the highest weighted F1-score on KITTI, and removing the final SWAP gates reduces circuit complexity. Under noise, the ranking of configurations changes, with IQFT-After degrading more.

entry.title: Geometry of Magic Robustness and Directed State Conversion
entry.summary: Beyond Robustness of Magic: Quantifying Quantum State Convertibility arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces a state-space distance calibrated by stabilizer states, based on the dual structure of the robustness of magic (RoM), and shows that RoM equals the distance to the set of free states. It extends this geometry to state conversion by defining a directed conversion deficiency, the distance from a target state to the states freely reachable from a given input. For single-qubit systems, the authors analytically construct a continuous family of mixed states with identical RoM but asymmetric convertibility.

entry.title: Certified quantum phase diagrams: a quantum algorithm that verifiably maps phase transitions without order parameters or training data
entry.summary: Certified Discovery of Quantum Phase Diagrams arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper asks whether a machine can provably discover new quantum phases of matter under physically motivated assumptions. For smooth families of geometrically local Hamiltonians, it constructs an efficient quantum algorithm that outputs the phase diagram to prescribed accuracy and certifies each reported transition. The algorithm uses only a classical Hamiltonian description and unverified reference ground states, detecting energy-gap closing with a frequency-filtered local probe, and also gives a quasipolynomial-time classical algorithm. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose certified quantum-algorithmic phase diagram discovery via frequency-filtered probes detecting gap closing; numerical experiments on several models are reported.

entry.title: Security Proof for Strong Quantum Pseudorandom Unitaries at Birthday-Scale Query Limits
entry.summary: Birthday-Scale Non-Adaptive Security for Strong Pseudorandom Unitaries arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies strong pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs), where an adversary may also access U†, U*, and U^T. The authors prove that the DPFC candidate construction resists about √N non-adaptive queries for an N-dimensional unitary, matching the best known bound for non-strong PRUs and improving on earlier strong-PRU analyses. They also show that in the adaptive setting, DPFC cannot remain secure when the number of queries is much larger than √N. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine EPR-sector decomposition with path-recording to prove birthday-scale non-adaptive security for DPFC strong PRUs, plus an adaptive upper bound.

entry.title: Clifford Hierarchy Gates from Clifford Stabilizers in 2D
entry.summary: The Clifford Hierarchy from Clifford Stabilizers in 2D arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies logical gates in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes. The Bravyi-König theorem restricts constant-depth logical gates to the Clifford group. The authors show that two-dimensional topological codes with Clifford stabilizers can realize transversal logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy. They give two constructions based on quantum doubles of D4 and Z2, with k logical qubits and a logical C^(k-1)Z gate at level k, implemented using only physical Z or CZ gates. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct 2D topological codes with Clifford stabilizers realizing transversal logical C^(k-1)Z gates at arbitrary Clifford hierarchy levels, using quantum doubles of D4 and Z2.

entry.title: Convex splitting via binary quantum hypothesis testing: bounding how many quantum systems are needed to hide a correlated one
entry.summary: Convex splitting by binary quantum hypothesis testing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper asks how many independent quantum systems are needed to hide one system correlated with a reference. It converts any joint measurement on all systems and the reference into binary tests on a single system and the reference. The resulting bounds apply to density operators on separable Hilbert spaces and are applied to one-shot private communication and one-way secret key distillation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recast convex splitting via binary hypothesis tests, derive one-shot bounds for private communication and key distillation, and report Gaussian corrections with a log n remainder.

entry.title: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines
entry.summary: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a higher-order neuromorphic Ising machine that enforces constraints through programmable state transitions instead of energy penalties. A compiler converts parity, cardinality, one-hot, partition and permutation constraints into wiring whose auxiliary clause count grows polynomially. On third-order graph matching, the machine needs orders of magnitude fewer iterations than penalty-based neuromorphic machines, and it is also configured on an FPGA to decode the surface code. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors compile constraints into programmable state transitions instead of energy penalties, and report validation on third-order graph matching and surface-code decoding against penalty-based mac

entry.title: Linking silicon nitride nanophotonics with cuprous oxide Rydberg excitons
entry.summary: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper couples Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu2O) to a silicon nitride (SiNx) nanophotonic waveguide in a monolithic, CMOS-compatible design. Under non-resonant excitation, emission from a Cu2O microcrystal couples into the guided mode, travels along the waveguide, and is collected at an output grating. The spectrum shows phonon-assisted 1s orthoexciton emission along with the 2p and 3p lines of the yellow Rydberg series.

entry.title: Attributing surface-code failures under non-Pauli noise depends on how trajectories are paired
entry.summary: Counterfactual attribution of surface-code failures under non-Pauli noise: dependence on trajectory pairing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies how to attribute a quantum error-correction failure to the noise that caused it when the noise is non-Pauli. It defines a failing shot's cause set as the sites whose removal alone eliminates the failure, and separates this from effects that do not depend on the pairing choice. In a distance-three surface code, exact non-Pauli noise and its Pauli twirl fail at comparable rates, yet their attributions differ markedly under shared random draws.

entry.title: Ising-encoded computational homogenization: treating stress as a quantum observable
entry.summary: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents an energy-based variational quantum method for linear-elastic computational homogenization. The representative volume element's finite-element energy is written as a QUBO problem and mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian, whose ground state encodes the equilibrium fluctuation field. Using the Hellmann–Feynman theorem, differentiating with respect to macroscopic strain yields stress observables whose expectation values match the volume-averaged homogenized stress. These observables are one-local and diagonal in the same computational basis, so they can be measured alongside the energy.

entry.title: Curvature-calibrated friction and an exact gauge symmetry for quantum Hamiltonian descent
entry.summary: Curvature-Calibrated Friction and an Exact Gauge Symmetry for Quantum Hamiltonian Descent arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies solving PDE-constrained design problems on a quantum computer using Quantum Hamiltonian Descent. It identifies two obstacles in the pipeline: covariance generators violate the positivity conditions required by the oracle, which is repaired by an affine combination of positive semidefinite atoms, and the mean-objective friction heuristic breaks a constant-shift invariance. Calibrating friction to landscape curvature restores this symmetry.

entry.title: Generating cat states with a superconducting two-photon Jaynes-Cummings circuit
entry.summary: Generation of coherent-state Schrödinger cat states in a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model implemented with Josephson junctions arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how to create Schrödinger cat states, superpositions of coherent states, using a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model built from Josephson-junction circuits. The authors estimate the coupling strength for a superconducting flux qubit and numerically simulate flux noise, energy relaxation, and photon loss. They find that photon loss strongly reduces cat-state fidelity. The paper also examines phase-state dynamics for several photon numbers and how the initial temperature affects fidelity and the Wigner function.

entry.title: Quantum transitions at a separatrix in classical phase space, extending the QKNH theorem beyond double wells
entry.summary: Quantum dynamical transitions when the corresponding classical phase space has a separatrix: extension of the QKNH theorem beyond double wells arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper extends the quantum version of the Kruskal-Neishtadt-Henrard theorem (QKNH) beyond double-well systems. It studies a slowly driven quantum pendulum, where avoided crossings arise from reflection above the potential barrier rather than tunneling through it. The authors show that the resulting Landau-Zener probabilities have the same local lattice form as in the double-well problem, so the QKNH theorem can be applied.

entry.title: How well emergent-Hamiltonian quantum memories hold up against noise
entry.summary: Resilience of emergent Hamiltonian quantum memories in the presence of noise arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how robust quantum memories built from emergent Hamiltonians are when noise is present. The authors show that the storage spectrum can be tuned to a noisy environment without changing the stored entangled state. For Bell-pair products prepared from density waves, a selection rule blocks local density noise from linking the target state to its degenerate partners. The paper also reports storage-time behavior under 1/f and Ohmic noise and treats fermionic loss as a solvable model.

entry.title: Certified gap between coherent and adaptive temporal processing in quantum error-correction readout
entry.summary: Certified Separation Between Coherent and Adaptive Temporal Processing of Quantum-Error-Correction Readout arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies how repeated quantum error-correction readout signals should be processed over time, comparing storing only classical measurement records with preserving quantum information between rounds. It frames the question as a loss-weighted state-discrimination problem. In an idealized two-round benchmark with QPSK signals, a receiver with a seven-dimensional persistent register achieves a certified lower recovery-decision error than any adaptive receiver.

entry.title: Tunable source of entangled microwaves made by nonlinear magnon scattering
entry.summary: Tunable source of entangled microwaves by nonlinear scattering of magnons arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes generating entangled microwaves in separate transmission lines using the nonlinear dynamics of spin waves (magnons) in ferromagnetic films. A driven magnon mode produces entangled magnon pairs through three-magnon down-conversion, and film anisotropy amplifies only one specific pair of modes. Each amplified mode is coupled out to its own microwave line. Changing the orientation of the bias magnetic field tunes the frequency difference between the two microwaves across a few-GHz range.

entry.title: Analysis and numerical study of a proposed nonlinear extension to quantum mechanics
entry.summary: Analytic and Numerical Investigation of a Proposed Non-linear Extension of Quantum Mechanics arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines further properties of a nonlinear extension of quantum mechanics introduced earlier. The authors show analytically that the model reduces to ordinary linear quantum mechanics in a certain limit. They also carry out a perturbation analysis around an exact solution from earlier work, and use Floquet theory to study a system under periodic driving. Numerical comparisons between the exact solution and the analytic approximation show how nonlinear effects change particle trajectories, especially near the linear limit.

entry.title: Review: Isotopes for medicine and fundamental physics
entry.summary: Colloquium: Isotopes for medicine and fundamental physics arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This review covers techniques for enriching and detecting isotopes, variants of elements distinguished by neutron number, and their uses in medicine and basic science. It opens with challenges posed by Maxwell, Rutherford, and Einstein and traces the development of isotope separation methods. It also discusses radioisotopes for cancer therapy, stable isotopes as metabolic tracers, and proposed tests of quantum mechanics using radioactive atomic clocks.

entry.title: Characterizing a remotely accessible neutral-atom quantum simulator
entry.summary: Characterizing a neutral atom quantum simulator accessible in cloud arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies Fresnel, a cloud-accessible neutral-atom analog quantum simulator provided by Pasqal. The authors run experiments testing how the machine responds to different pulse sequences and settings, and identify the main noise sources affecting its dynamics. From this data they build an effective model of the system's noisy evolution and use numerical optimization to infer the noise strengths. The model accurately reproduces the simulator's dynamics.

entry.title: A Quantum Continuous Wavelet Transform (a quantum method for analyzing a signal's scale and position together)
entry.summary: A Quantum Continuous Wavelet Transform arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper constructs a quantum continuous wavelet transform on a finite scale-translation grid that allows non-dyadic scales. It uses a quantum Fourier transform, a block-encoded scale-dependent multiplier with a flag qubit, and an inverse transform to produce complex wavelet coefficients in the success branch. The authors bound the success probability, show the bound is attained under a frequency-conditioned scale preparation, and provide a resource estimate. They also show that Fourier-basis measurement reproduces the scale outcomes exactly, while the QCWT adds information in the joint scale-translation distribution.

entry.title: Generalizing and combining check constructions for fault-tolerant quantum state preparation
entry.summary: Generalizing and Combining Check Constructions: Design-Space Exploration for Fault-Tolerant Quantum State Preparation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper introduces Block Checks, in which several checks share one fault-tolerantly prepared auxiliary block, placing them and existing constructions in a single design space. It also proposes a Pareto tree search that adds checks and auxiliary blocks, merges auxiliaries, and edits circuits to explore this space. On quantum codes of distance up to seven, the search finds best-known circuits for many new operation-depth trade-offs and outperforms existing methods. The code is open source as part of the Munich Quantum Toolkit (MQT).

entry.title: Agentic MLIR-to-QIR Translation Using Dual-Backend Testing and a Hybrid Deterministic and LLM Approach
entry.summary: Agentic MLIR-to-QIR Translation with Dual-Backend Testing: A Hybrid Deterministic and LLM Approach arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Each quantum framework defines its own MLIR dialect, so moving a circuit to a QIR runtime normally requires a hand-written pass for every dialect. This paper presents a translator that chooses between a deterministic compiler path for known dialects, an LLM agentic path for unseen dialects, and a repair path when deterministic output fails testing. Source and generated circuits are run on independent simulators and their output distributions are compared by total variation distance. Across 41 circuits in three dialects, the deterministic path matched gates exactly on all 70 circuit-dialect pairs, with average similarity above 95%.

entry.title: A measurement-free error correction method for superconducting microwave cavities
entry.summary: A measurement-free quantum error correction protocol for superconducting cavities arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper adapts a measurement-free quantum error correction protocol, originally proposed for photon loss, to a circuit quantum electrodynamics setup. Three superconducting microwave cavities coupled through Josephson-junction nonlinear elements are used, with the logical qubit encoded in the lowest-order binomial code of one cavity and the other two cavities serving as ancillas. Numerical simulations with experimentally realistic parameters show single-photon loss can be corrected with 99% fidelity, extending the logical lifetime by a factor of 1.2 to 1.8 over unprotected Fock encoding.

entry.title: Self-testing in fermionic networks: certifying quantum states from correlations alone
entry.summary: Self-testing in Fermionic Networks arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Self-testing certifies quantum states and measurements using only observed correlations, without assumptions about the devices' internal workings. This paper shows that modeling devices as qudits or as febits (information encoded in fermion presence or absence) affects self-testing results, since some correlations uniquely fix a qudit strategy yet admit two inequivalent fermionic realizations. The authors develop a fermionic self-testing framework. They show that correlations from a three-party rewiring network single out febit states and measurements up to local parity-preserving isometries, providing the first genuine fermionic self-test.

entry.title: Modeling couplings and quench dynamics in 100-qubit quantum processors
entry.summary: Modeling couplings and quench dynamics of hundred-qubit quantum processors arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper derives effective Hamiltonians for two-dimensional superconducting quantum processors using continuous unitary transformations, at a cost polynomial in qubit number. For a 96-transmon array with tunable couplers, it extracts effective couplings, state-dependent interactions such as ZZ couplings, and eigenstate locality, taking at most an hour per design point on one GPU. Combined with semiclassical sampling, the authors predict quench dynamics of 100 qubits and 180 couplers at half filling and validate the method against exact dynamics of smaller arrays.

entry.title: Quantum many-body scars and zero modes in the spin-1 Kitaev chain
entry.summary: Quantum many-body scars and zero modes in the spin-1 Kitaev chain arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies the spin-1 Kitaev chain and shows, by analyzing its Hilbert-space connectivity in the Cartesian basis, that it hosts exponentially many exact zero-energy modes protected by chiral symmetry. For even-length periodic chains, the number of these modes is lower-bounded by the Jacobsthal number (2^{L+1}+1)/3. The authors also construct zero modes with analytic expressions and identify an embedded tight-binding structure governing defect dynamics that supports PXP-like quantum many-body scars in several previously unreported sectors.

entry.title: A kernel method for learning quantum phases using basis-dependent features
entry.summary: A Basis-Dependent Kernel for Learning Quantum Phases of Matter arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces the inverse participation ratio (IPR) kernel, a method for learning quantum phases of matter from IPRs in physically motivated bases. Unlike fidelity-based kernels, it can identify physically meaningful similarity between orthogonal states. The method is tested on ground states of the transverse-field Ising and Heisenberg XXZ models. For TFIM Gibbs states, it retains phase-relevant structure over a range of nonzero temperatures where fidelity-based kernels degrade.

entry.title: Passive memories beyond the Ising model: from SFQ to GKP explained
entry.summary: Passive memories beyond the Ising model: from SFQ to GKP arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper reviews how two classical passive memories work: flash memory, which traps charge on a conducting island, and flux storage in a superconducting loop used in single-flux quantum logic. It draws analogies to charge and flux qubits and notes that protection comes from a large, tunable energy barrier that can be suppressed during writing. The authors introduce a 2D floating XY model and study a self-dual superconducting circuit that hosts GKP codewords as symmetry-broken ground states, discussing its protection and limitations.

entry.title: Particle scattering off superconducting qubits, from single devices to arrays
entry.summary: Theory of Particle Scattering on Superconducting Qubits: From Single Devices to Quantum Arrays arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper develops a general framework for inelastic scattering, in which an incident particle exchanges a virtual photon with a superconducting circuit and drives a transition between its internal states. The authors build a realistic electrostatic response model for planar Xmon-style transmon qubits and apply it to photon-mediated scattering of eV-scale bosonic dark matter. They report that this substantially improves projected sensitivity at the lowest masses. The paper also states that the rate scales with N for independent qubits and can approach N² for suitably prepared Dicke states when spatial coherence is maintained.

entry.title: Quantum speedup for diffusion maps: spectral filters and Galerkin PDE solvers
entry.summary: Accelerating Diffusion Maps on a Quantum Computer: Spectral Filtering and Galerkin PDE Solvers arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a quantum algorithm framework for accelerating diffusion maps, a nonlinear generalization of principal component analysis used for dimensionality reduction and PDE approximation on point clouds. It avoids explicitly building the graph Laplacian by using a symmetric factorization at the block-encoding level, combining Gaussian moment dilation, Laplace-weighted LCU, and QSVT to implement spectral filters. The authors report that under polylogarithmic-cost oracle access, their heat-overlap algorithm achieves O(polylog N) gate complexity, validated with ideal statevector simulations and a benchmark showing a quadratic precision advantage for energy readout.

entry.title: Learning integer winding times for more accurate quantum phase estimation
entry.summary: Learning Integer Winding Evolution Times in Quantum Phase Estimation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes learning the Hamiltonian evolution time in Quantum Phase Estimation so that the measured phase distribution has low Shannon entropy. An optimization loop minimizes the entropy of the measured eigenvalues, which greatly improves minimum eigenvalue accuracy, as shown numerically on quantum magnet models. The authors present this as the first introduction of parameter learning into QPE, making it more practical near term by allowing shorter-depth circuits.

entry.title: Entanglement inequalities for pure states, derived from graph structures
entry.summary: Entanglement Geometry Beyond Polygons: Graph-Theoretic Entanglement Inequalities arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how entanglement entropies of pure multipartite quantum states are constrained when subsystem cuts are organized as edges of graphs or hyperedges of hypergraphs. Starting from the one-party entanglement polygon inequality, the authors derive these constraints from strong subadditivity and pure-state complementarity, with optimal coefficients and equality conditions. The work also covers optimal polygon coefficients for weighted families of cuts and examines deficits and saturation for paths, overlapping hyperchains, and cluster states.

entry.title: How problem structure shapes single-layer QAOA performance
entry.summary: The Pre-Optimization Structure of QAOA: Polynomial Equivalence of Average and Optimal Probabilities arXiv · Oct 22, 2026This paper formalizes problem structure in single-layer QAOA as a joint probability distribution over the coarsest partition of the computational basis, defined by cost values and mixer-dependent walk counts. It proves a mean-max non-separation bound linking parameter-averaged target probability to its variational maximum. An exact matrix inner-product expression is derived and illustrated with transverse field and Grover mixers.

entry.title: Fast exact simulation of realistic noise for fault-tolerant quantum error correction circuits
entry.summary: QuasiStim: Scalable Accurate Non-Pauli Noise Simulation for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits arXiv · Oct 12, 2026This paper presents QuasiStim, a framework for exactly simulating realistic non-Pauli noise, such as coherent control errors, in fault-tolerant quantum error correction circuits instead of approximating it with Pauli twirling. It consists of QuasiFold, which merges equivalent non-Pauli noise sites to reduce the number of shots, and DeltaFrame, which samples from precomputed reference trajectories. The authors report over 100× fewer shots on bivariate-bicycle codes and 166× to 1331× speedups over a per-shot tableau simulator on rotated surface-code memory.

entry.title: Collective quantum state preparation is nonadditive, meaning joint preparation can beat separate optimal runs
entry.summary: Collective Shortcuts for Preparing Identical Qubits arXiv · Oct 5, 2026The paper studies the resource cost of preparing many quantum states together under weighted Pauli control, where rotations are charged by angle. It derives the exact single-qubit cost and shows a four-pulse collective protocol prepares two T states more cheaply than two optimal single-copy protocols. The authors also identify Bloch-sphere regions with collective savings and give a dimension-independent Rényi-entropy speed limit.

entry.title: A quantum master equation that keeps detailed balance and has second-order error bounds
entry.summary: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Second-order Error Bound arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper constructs a nonsecular quantum master equation for open quantum systems that satisfies time-reversal Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (TR-KMS) detailed balance, inherited from microscopic reversibility. Under suitable conditions, the authors prove that the difference between predicted and exact reduced density matrices is bounded by O(λ²) uniformly in time, where λ is the system-bath coupling strength. In a benchmark with two coupled oscillators, the equation keeps O(λ²) accuracy in both secular and nonsecular regimes and outperforms the other detailed-balance equations tested. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct a nonsecular master equation with TR-KMS detailed balance, report a time-uniform O(λ²) error bound, and validate it on a two-oscillator benchmark.

entry.title: Limits of magic-state cultivation: which faults harm non-Clifford state preparation
entry.summary: The limits of magic-state cultivation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper develops an exact theory of which faults are harmful in circuits that prepare magic states with non-Clifford gates and postselection, such as magic-state cultivation. It shows that a single stabilizer code on the non-Clifford gates determines harmful faults, linking cultivation to distillation and bounding the T-count from below. The authors also show that using S gates as a proxy for T gates can only overstate the fault distance of such checks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors develop an exact theory identifying harmful faults via one stabilizer code, giving a T-count lower bound and analyzing magic-state cultivation checks.

entry.title: On reaction depth and fast fault-tolerant Boolean logic (paper on classical-coprocessor consultations in quantum programs)
entry.summary: On Reaction Depth and Fast Fault-Tolerant Boolean Logic arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper formalizes “reaction depth,” the number of times a classical coprocessor must be consulted while running a quantum program, and examines subtleties in this theory. It focuses on coherent Boolean logic and uses a gateset of homogeneous Z- and X-type Pauli product measurements plus Toffoli states. The authors prove that any Boolean arithmetic circuit can be implemented with constant quantum depth and constant reaction depth, at the cost of exponential space. They also present efficient AutoAND, ripple-carry adder, and schoolbook multiplier implementations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize reaction depth, prove any Boolean arithmetic circuit has constant quantum and reaction depth, and give efficient adder and multiplier constructions.

entry.title: A provably efficient classical method for simulating first-order OTOCs in 1D
entry.summary: A provably efficient classical algorithm for simulating OTOC⁽¹⁾ in 1D arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces "window propagation," a classical algorithm for approximating first-order out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) in 1D Haar-random brickwork circuits. The authors prove it runs in polynomial time at arbitrary depths, with inverse-polynomial mean-squared error. Numerical experiments compare its results with exact computation on Clifford circuits with up to 512 qubits and 768 T-gates, and on Haar-random circuits with up to 22 qubits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce window propagation, claiming the first provably polynomial-time classical approximation of first-order OTOCs in 1D Haar brickwork circuits, with numerical comparisons up to 512 q

entry.title: Measurement-order dependence and limits on quantum uncertainty, contextuality, steering and Bell violations
entry.summary: Measurement-order dependence bounds uncertainty, contextuality, steering, and Bell nonlocality arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper measures how much the outcome statistics change when two quantum measurements are performed in opposite orders, using total-variation, Jensen-Shannon and Hellinger distances. These order scores vanish when the measurements commute. The authors use them to bound violations of noncontextuality, steering and Bell inequalities. ★★★★ Notable: The authors bound Bell violations bilinearly by order-record distances, prove the bound for one party with up to three settings, and conjecture it in general.

entry.title: Impossibility theorems for ordered universal entanglement purification
entry.summary: No-Go Theorems for Ordered Universal Entanglement Purification arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies whether nontrivial universal entanglement purification is possible for a finite set of pairs with ordered fidelities, using separable operations. For each fixed number of inputs, it shows that when independently prepared two-qubit pairs range over all states above a fixed fidelity threshold, any successful map that never lowers the highest input fidelity must preserve that fidelity exactly. This rules out nontrivial universal LOCC purification even at arbitrarily high input fidelities. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a no-go theorem for ordered universal purification under separable operations, for every finite n and arbitrarily high input fidelity.

entry.title: Long-distance continuous-variable entanglement distribution over deployed fibre
entry.summary: Long-distance continuous variable entanglement distribution over deployed fibre arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper demonstrates distributing continuous-variable entanglement over deployed metropolitan optical fibre. The two modes of a two-mode squeezed vacuum state are sent to remote nodes through 23 km (about 7 dB loss) and 450 m (about 1 dB loss) fibre links, each using an independent free-running laser and a polarisation-diverse coherent receiver.
