Digital recovery of timing, phase and polarisation uses co-propagating pilot tones, and inter-mode correlations align the quadratures. The entanglement is certified by a Simon-Duan value of 1.915 ± 0.013, below the separability bound of 2, and a logarithmic negativity of 0.067 ± 0.011. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report distributing CV entanglement over deployed metro fibre using digital recovery of phase, polarisation and timing, verified via Simon-Duan and log negativity.

entry.title: Topological origin of directional amplification in higher-dimensional non-Hermitian lattices
entry.summary: Topological Origin of Directional Amplification in Arbitrary-Dimensional Non-Hermitian Lattices arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies directional amplification in non-Hermitian lattices, where gain, loss and nonreciprocal couplings can produce exponentially growing responses. Using the concept of the amoeba, the logarithmic image of the singularities of the response generating function, the authors build a framework valid in any dimension. They show that the asymptotic response is determined by the component of the amoeba's complement extending toward negative infinity, giving a general topological criterion for whether directional amplification occurs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use amoeba connected components to give a dimension-independent topological criterion for directional amplification in non-Hermitian lattices.

entry.title: Fast exact noisy quantum circuit sampling with mid-circuit measurements and general noise channels
entry.summary: General Noise Channels and Mid-Circuit Measurements for Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper generalizes pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution (PTSBE) to noisy quantum circuits with mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels, without approximation. Implemented on GPUs as a CUDA-Q extension, it reports speedups of up to 24x over conventional CUDA-Q trajectory sampling on distance-3 topological code memories and up to 83x over the Clifft simulator on 30-qubit random circuits. The authors also find that Pauli twirling of amplitude damping overestimates the detection rate by 21% and raises a lookup decoder's logical error rate by 8% on a surface-code memory. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend pre-trajectory sampling to mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels, reporting speedups over CUDA-Q and Clifft on GPUs.

entry.title: A fault-tolerant quantum chip needing few external control wires
entry.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by classical processors, where quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked planar array of local gates. The chip receives classical instructions through a small, constant number of external wires, while other qubits evolve under a fixed, periodically applied depth-3 local circuit. Assuming a noiseless global clock, the authors establish an accuracy threshold theorem. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a fault-tolerant quantum processor with few external wires and a fixed depth-3 local circuit, and report an accuracy threshold theorem.

entry.title: Standard adiabatic quantum optimization may gain a subexponential speedup
entry.summary: Vanilla Adiabatic Quantum Optimization Can Have Subexponential Advantage arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper constructs a family of objective functions for which standard adiabatic quantum optimization, evolving under a given Hamiltonian, finds the global minimizer in polynomial time. In the black-box model, the authors state that any classical algorithm needs exp(n^Ω(1)) time for the same task. The result replaces the linearization technique used in an earlier work by Leng et al., which used a transverse field Ising mixer. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a construction giving subexponential quantum advantage for vanilla adiabatic optimization in the black-box model, replacing the prior linearization technique with a new one.

entry.title: Frequency stability of periodic Ramsey sampling under a drifting shift
entry.summary: Residual Allan Stability under Periodic Auxiliary Ramsey Sampling arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies how the timing of auxiliary Ramsey measurements affects the frequency stability linked to a drifting pulse shift, holding the nominal Fisher-information rate fixed. For periodic instantaneous observations of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck shift with causal prediction between updates, it derives the exact residual covariance averaged over the update cycle and the Allan variance at arbitrary averaging times. Compared with a continuous Kalman reference at the same information rate, periodic estimation increases the cycle-averaged estimation-error variance and reduces the short-time residual Allan variance, but increases its long-time value.

entry.title: Quantum information processing with dressed-state qubits on a multilayer ion trap chip
entry.summary: Dressed-State Quantum Information Processing Using a Multilayer Ion Trap Chip with an Integrated Radio Frequency Resonator arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper experimentally demonstrates radio frequency (RF)-dressed-state qubit preparation, coherent operation of a single dressed qubit, and selective readout of dressed hyperfine states in 171Yb+ ions. The authors designed and fabricated a multilayer microstructured ion trap chip with an integrated resonator that creates an RF magnetic field amplitude gradient along a linear ion crystal. This gradient enables individual addressing and coupling of dressed qubits. Individual addressing is shown in a two-ion Coulomb crystal using a global modulated RF field near 12.6 GHz.

entry.title: Residual-algebra design method for symmetry-preserving variational quantum circuits
entry.summary: Residual-Algebraic Design of Symmetry-Preserving Variational Quantum Circuits arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies symmetry-preserving variational quantum circuits. It shows that preserving symmetry alone does not ensure accessibility within the target symmetry sector, and uses a residual dynamical Lie algebra and its commutant to identify invariant blocks in that sector. The block populations are conserved and give a kinematic upper bound on fidelity with a target state. The authors propose screening candidate generators before variational optimization and demonstrate the approach on the XXZ and Hubbard models.

entry.title: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN Framework for Reliable Superconducting Quantum Compilation
entry.summary: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents CREST, a graph neural network framework that scores how well a quantum circuit matches each candidate region of a superconducting processor before routing. It combines gate dependencies and logical-qubit interactions with each region's connectivity and calibration attributes, and is trained using real-device execution outcomes. On 324 circuits from seven datasets on TianYan-176, CREST improves mean measurement-distribution fidelity by 19.03% over the strongest baseline. Using updated calibration data, the same model keeps the highest overall mean fidelity across six measurement dates without retraining.

entry.title: A quantum method for molecular chemistry using a sum-of-squares representation
entry.summary: Quantum Simulation of First-Quantised Chemistry with a Sum-of-Squares Representation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a first-quantised phase estimation algorithm for computing molecular energies, based on a non-convex sum-of-squares representation of the Hamiltonian and spectral-gap amplification. It is compared against the state-of-the-art second-quantised algorithm, with both compiled using the same logical-level techniques. For six molecules, the method needs up to 16 times fewer Toffoli gates in the low-qubit regime and uses a smallest qubit count 1.4 to 2 times lower.

entry.title: Estimating the Hurst exponent with quantum wavelets, a method for measuring the roughness of random paths
entry.summary: Hurst Exponent Estimation with Quantum Wavelets arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how accurately the Hurst exponent of fractional Brownian motion can be estimated from repeated measurements of one amplitude-encoded path. The authors extend a quantum nondecimated wavelet transform, adding mirror extension to remove the endpoint jump and deriving the sampling distribution of the estimator. They compare readout methods at equal query budgets, reporting lower error for mirroring and for direct measurement in the studied settings.

entry.title: Time-varying medium built from laser-driven quantum emitters
entry.summary: Time-Varying Medium from an Ensemble of Laser-Dressed Quantum Emitters arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a minimal quantum-mechanical model of a frequency-dispersive, time-modulated medium made of a homogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters driven by a pump laser. The authors derive the ensemble's macroscopic polarizability and solve Maxwell's equations using the Floquet formalism. The results show a band structure that differs from conventional analyses that neglect the modulation source, arising from the interplay between dispersive polaritonic and time-varying responses.

entry.title: Detecting quantum non-classicality with free electrons by witnessing Wigner negativity
entry.summary: Shedding Light on Quantum Non-Classicality: Witnessing Wigner Negativity with Free Electrons arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a noise-resilient framework for witnessing Wigner negativity, a signature of quantum non-classicality in light, using phase-resolved quantum photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (QPINEM). It maps electron coherences to optical characteristic functions within a coupling-limited phase-space region, avoiding full optical state reconstruction. A witness matrix built from recorded electron spectra via Bochner's theorem certifies non-classicality when it has negative eigenvalues. The protocol is benchmarked on vacuum-Fock superpositions, odd cat states, and GKP states.

entry.title: Environment-assisted imaginary time evolution for feedback-based quantum algorithms
entry.summary: Environment-assisted imaginary time evolution in feedback-based quantum algorithms arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper improves the FALQON algorithm, which finds ground states of quantum systems without classical parameter tuning but can get stuck. The authors describe imaginary time evolution as an operation induced by an environment and combine it with the FALQON feedback law. In simulations of the ANNNI frustrated Ising chain and the MaxCut problem, the method prepares ground states from any initial state and needs fewer layers on average for fixed initial states.

entry.title: Squeezed cooling and lasing with cold atoms in cavity QED
entry.summary: Squeezed Cooling and Lasing with Cold Atoms in Cavity-QED arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes an optical squeezed laser built from rubidium atom ensembles coupled to a squeezed cavity mode via cavity-assisted Raman transitions, requiring no nonlinear crystal or injected squeezed light. A first ensemble cools the cavity into a squeezed vacuum, reaching up to 9 dB of intracavity squeezing and 18 dB of output squeezing. Incoherently pumping a second ensemble drives lasing into the squeezed mode, producing a bright beam with long coherence time and noise below the vacuum level.

entry.title: Memory cost of compressing entanglement spectra with magic
entry.summary: The magical memory cost of entanglement spectrum compression arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper asks how much quantum memory is needed to faithfully keep the entanglement spectrum of a bipartite pure state after Bell pairs are separated out by local unitaries. It derives an exact tradeoff between Bell-pair yield, residual memory, and reconstruction fidelity, and defines an operational measure of entanglement-spectrum complexity. Smoothed entanglement spread gives a lower bound on this memory cost, while diverging nonlocal magic forces unbounded memory at any fixed positive fidelity.

entry.title: Magnetometry using both coherent signal and thermal fluctuations in cavity-magnon systems
entry.summary: Coherent-Response and Thermal-Fluctuation Information in Cavity-Magnon Magnetometry arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper shows that the variance of a measured microwave quadrature in cavity-magnon systems carries magnetic-field information beyond the usual coherent response. The authors derive a Gaussian likelihood and show its Fisher information splits exactly into a coherent-displacement term and a thermal-fluctuation term. They identify distinct optimal operating conditions for each term and map how drive frequency, drive strength, and temperature shift their relative contributions.

entry.title: Instanton tunnelling as a checkable benchmark for digital quantum simulation on quantum hardware
entry.summary: Instanton tunnelling as a verifiable benchmark for digital quantum simulation: circuit structure, classical simulability and hardware reproducibility arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper uses instanton-mediated tunnelling in a quartic double well as a benchmark for digital quantum simulation that can be checked against an exact answer. A unary encoding maps N lattice sites to N qubits, and a second-order Trotter circuit is shown to have Schmidt rank at most four across any cut, independent of N. Matrix-product-state simulations reproduce the exact splitting up to N = 48. Measurements on two superconducting processors at N = 8 recover the lattice splitting to a few percent, and repeated runs show reproducibility that depends on the time between sessions.

entry.title: Entangling photon number states using a quantum memory interferometer
entry.summary: Number-correlated photon entanglement with a quantum memory interferometer arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes embedding a quantum memory within a Mach-Zehnder interferometer to convert single-mode photon states into number-correlated entangled states. It uses off-resonant ladder-type atomic interaction to map single-photon excitations onto photon pairs without conventional optical nonlinearities. The authors also describe applications including photonic non-demolition detection, state preparation, and frequency conversion.

entry.title: Gutzwiller quantum-classical embedding for simulating electron dynamics
entry.summary: Gutzwiller Quantum-Classical Embedding for Dynamics Simulations of Correlated Electron Systems arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces t-GQCE, a time-dependent Gutzwiller quantum-classical embedding framework for simulating real-time dynamics of correlated electrons in multi-orbital lattice models. A classical computer propagates a noninteracting quasiparticle lattice, while quantum processors propagate finite interacting embedding models, exchanging only Hamiltonian parameters and single-particle density matrices. The method is demonstrated on interaction quenches in the Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice, using quantum hardware and noise-model simulations.

entry.title: A local hidden-variable model for postselected EPR correlations
entry.summary: On a local hidden-variable model for postselected EPR correlations arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a theoretical and numerical analysis of a Bell-type experiment using a sigmoid-based threshold model for linear polarization measurements on nonmaximally entangled two-qubit states. The model violates the fair-sampling assumption required by the CHSH inequality. Simulations examine how closely this local construction reproduces quantum-like correlations in the postselected detected sample across a range of entanglement parameters. In the tested configurations, CHSH-type violations appear only in that postselected sample, through a setting-dependent detection mechanism.

entry.title: A Relativistic Quantum Mechanical Formulation of Wu-Shaknov Entanglements
entry.summary: A Relativistic Quantum Mechanical Formulation of Wu-Shaknov Entanglements arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper proposes that quantum entanglement forms spontaneously between spin, helicity, and polarization states in creation and annihilation processes. Using an earlier framework for describing free particle-antiparticle pairs of any spin in a unified relativistic quantum mechanical way, the authors give a comprehensive formulation of Wu-Shaknov entanglements. Under certain theoretical assumptions, they derive relationships between amplitudes and Born-like probabilities for incoming and outgoing states, and examine how these behave under a dynamical group meant to supply correlations across spacetime frames. The authors suggest that a modified version of some conventional conservation laws could provide general selection rules for relativistic entanglement formation.

entry.title: Sharp rank thresholds for entanglement in PPT extensions of symmetric quantum states
entry.summary: Sharp rank thresholds and cubic support in PPT extensions of completely symmetric states arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies completely symmetric quantum states on at least three parties with local rank at least three. It shows that the least rank of an entangled state passing any fixed finite positive level of the PPT extension hierarchy is 3d+N-3. At this rank, the two- and three-party marginals determine a plane cubic curve shared by all extensions. The authors also give conditions for the hierarchy to become exact at a finite level on this cubic, and an explicit rank-nine three-qutrit example.

entry.title: A quantum heat engine that improves performance by tuning interactions between bosons
entry.summary: A Bose-Hubbard quantum thermal machine arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes a quantum thermal machine made of interacting ultracold bosons in a one-dimensional optical lattice, described by the Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian. It uses an Otto-inspired cycle that adds strokes changing the interaction strength between bosons to the usual thermalization and compression/expansion strokes. The authors find that these interaction changes can enhance performance, outperforming non-interacting cycles.

entry.title: From BBM92 measurements to secure keys: practical implementation challenges
entry.summary: From BBM92 Measurements to Secure Keys: Challenges in a Practical Implementation arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines two implementations of the BBM92 quantum key distribution protocol: a conventional passive receiver and a time-multiplexed design that halves the number of detectors. The authors characterise the passive polarisation analysers used in both and report experiments with the time-multiplexed receiver, using a continuous-wave pumped entangled-photon source and threshold detectors. They also discuss difficulties in post-processing when trying to meet existing security proof requirements, and the gap between theoretical assumptions and extracting a provably secure key.

entry.title: Bound entanglement studied as a trigonometric moment problem
entry.summary: Bound entanglement as a trigonometric moment problem arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies entangled states that remain positive under partial transposition (PPT), focusing on a class of multiqubit states formed as real-weighted mixtures of products of equatorial spin coherent states. It recasts three questions (class membership, robustness to white noise, and minimal rank) as truncated trigonometric moment problems. Exact answers are given for several cases, including three-qubit states.

entry.title: HgCdTe avalanche photodiode photon counting and intrinsic dark current for quantum optics
entry.summary: Linear-mode photon counting performance and intrinsic dark current in HgCdTe APDs for quantum optical applications arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper characterizes HgCdTe avalanche photodiodes (APDs) for single-photon detection at 80 K, using a hybridized resistive transimpedance amplifier (RTIA) and a deported capacitive transimpedance amplifier (CTIA). In linear mode with gain above 400, the devices reached an external photon detection efficiency of 42% to 55% and a dark count rate of 2.6 MHz to 17 MHz. Using the CTIA, the authors measured gain-normalized dark current as low as 10.9 fA at gain 450, corresponding to a dark count rate of 150 Hz, and concluded that high dark counts are not an intrinsic limit of the technology.

entry.title: Virtual autopurification for purifying quantum states within one system
entry.summary: Virtual Autopurification in Translationally Invariant Quantum States arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper introduces virtual autopurification (VAP), a method for purifying quantum states that works within a single translationally invariant system. Instead of requiring multiple copies of the state, VAP builds virtual copies from spatially separated subregions and performs entangled measurements only between them. Under a clustering-of-correlations assumption, VAP reproduces the expectation values of standard virtual purification, with errors decaying exponentially in buffer length and inter-subregion distance. Numerical simulations support these predictions and show virtual cooling with reduced resource requirements.

entry.title: A unified method for the time-dependent quantum harmonic oscillator using point transformations and Lie symmetries
entry.summary: A unified approach to the time-dependent quantum harmonic oscillator via point transformations and Lie symmetries arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper revisits the time-dependent harmonic oscillator in quantum mechanics using equivalence transformations and Lie point symmetries. It gives the most general seven-parameter point transformations that map between the time-dependent and the ordinary harmonic oscillator, and reconstructs the Mehler kernel propagator for the time-independent case as a by-product. It also derives normalized wave functions by Lie algebraic methods, without using the Lewis–Riesenfeld invariant, and shows how the Lewis–Riesenfeld operator becomes a compatible second-order constraint on the SL(2,R)-invariant solutions.

entry.title: Doppler Effects on Satellite Time-Bin Quantum Key Distribution and a Ephemeris-Assisted Correction Method
entry.summary: Doppler effect on dual-downlink time-bin quantum key distribution and a proposed ephemeris-assisted witness-field correction arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how satellite motion causes Doppler shifts that disturb phase measurements in time-bin quantum key distribution to two ground stations. The authors propose an ephemeris-assisted scheme in which an auxiliary interferometer analyzes a co-propagating classical witness field to reconstruct each station's local Doppler phase, which is then compensated on the quantum channel. In a noise-free simulation, the correction keeps the phase-basis error rate below 2% and retains 93% of the ideal asymptotic key yield.

entry.title: Light emission from a quantum emitter near metallic or semiconducting atomic chains
entry.summary: Spontaneous emission of atomic systems near metallic and semiconducting atomic chains arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how a quantum emitter placed near finite atomic chains, modeled by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, emits light spontaneously. Dimerization tunes the chain from metallic to semiconducting, and the authors show how the scatterer's electronic structure and illumination determine the strength, bandwidth and spatial pattern of emission enhancement. Metallic chains give strong resonances, while semiconducting chains spread the response over a broader spectrum with lower peaks. The same mechanisms are also shown to persist in quasi-one-dimensional systems such as trans-polyacetylene chains and graphene nanoribbons.

entry.title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking Microarchitecture for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
entry.summary: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control arXiv · Nov 18, 2026Fault-tolerant quantum computing needs continuous error correction, and universal computation makes the controller update Pauli frames in real time based on measurement results. The paper presents QuFrame, a control microarchitecture that closes the error-correction loop within 1 microsecond using distributed instruction resolution engines, a lock-free frame management unit, and an on-chip fallback decoder that resolves in 144 nanoseconds.

entry.title: A convex-roof measure of quantum imaginarity based on affinity squares
entry.summary: A Convex-Roof Affinity-Square Measure of Quantum Imaginarity arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies quantum imaginarity, the part of a quantum state that cannot be written with real density matrices in a fixed basis. For pure states, it defines an affinity-square measure by minimizing over real states, obtaining a closed-form expression, and extends it to mixed states through a convex roof. The authors prove the extension is faithful, convex, and monotone under real operations. They also compute the convex roof exactly for arbitrary single-qubit mixed states.

entry.title: Quantifying extractable imaginarity using qubit triangles
entry.summary: Quantifying extractable imaginarity with qubit triangles arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper introduces a convex measure of quantum state imaginarity, defined as twice the area of a right triangle built from the input robustness and the largest conditional robustness. It derives computable bounds on this area in arbitrary finite dimensions and obtains exact values for certain classes of states. The authors show that two eight-dimensional states with identical robustness measures have different areas, which rules out deterministic conversion between them by real operations in one direction.

entry.title: Semiclassical Quantum Mechanics and Time-Varying Optics: A Theory of How Light's Frequency and Timing Change in Time-Modulated Media
entry.summary: Semiclassical Quantum Mechanics and the Optics of Time-Varying Media arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how rapid, high-contrast changes in optical properties such as refractive index reshape a light wave's frequency spectrum as it propagates. The authors draw an analogy with the non-commuting position and momentum operators of quantum mechanics, linking the theory to semiclassical quantum mechanics. They derive a non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation for wave propagation and a generalization of Hamilton's equations for the central frequency and arrival time of the wave spectrum.

entry.title: In-memory measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution
entry.summary: In-memory measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes a memory-assisted quantum key distribution protocol in which a stationary matter qubit and a travelling photonic qubit interfere inside a single quantum memory. Compared with memoryless MDI-QKD and existing two-memory designs, the scheme achieves higher secret key rates, beats the memoryless bound at shorter distances, and halves the number of memories and detectors. The authors identify off-resonant cascaded absorption (ORCA) memories as a promising platform for implementation.

entry.title: A relativistic gravitisation of quantum theory? A model linking quantum states to gravity in a relativistically causal way.
entry.summary: A relativistic gravitisation of quantum theory? arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper proposes a model called local semiclassical gravity, based on distributional semiclassical Einstein field equations sourced by the local quantum state, which updates through collapses only in the past light cone. In the weak-field limit the theory shows an explicitly causal dynamical structure, and in the nonrelativistic limit it recovers the Schrödinger-Newton equation. The authors analyse relativistic quantum measurements in this setup and argue they do not produce superluminal signalling, and they outline possible tabletop experiments to test the model.

entry.title: Gradient blind spots when adaptively searching IQP Born machine circuits
entry.summary: Gradient Blindness in Adaptive Architecture Search for IQP Born Machines arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies adaptive architecture search for IQP Born machines, quantum-style circuits of commuting gates that learn probability distributions from data. The authors show a candidate gate has nonzero gradient for some angles exactly when its generator is a sum of an odd number of linearly independent generators already in the circuit, so a seed of one-qubit gates never adds even-qubit gates. Adding the Chow-Liu tree edges to the seed lets the search see all candidates, matching full circuits on 12 and 16 qubits with 10 to 13 percent of the parameters. At 484 qubits, circuits grown from this seed reach lower test loss than a dense two-body circuit with 6 percent of its parameters.

entry.title: A quantum parallel algorithm for estimating products of many matrices' traces
entry.summary: Quantum Parallel Algorithm for Multivariate Trace Estimation with Applications arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm for estimating the multivariate trace Tr(A1A2...Ak) of several matrices, designed for near-term quantum devices. Matrices are accessed as vectorized states, and a tensor-network representation guides a parallel circuit whose depth does not depend on the number of matrices k, at the cost of qubit count growing linearly with k. The circuit can be distributed across O(k) devices. The authors apply it to spectral sum estimation and a quantum version of the Lanczos method, reducing circuit depth by the degree of the approximating polynomial for certain matrix classes.

entry.title: Stabilizer models for non-chiral abelian topological orders
entry.summary: Stabilizer models of achiral abelian topological orders arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper builds continuous-variable stabilizer codes that realize every achiral two-dimensional abelian topological order, for both bosonic and fermionic systems. Starting from any integer K-matrix with zero signature, the authors show that the corresponding topological order arises by condensing a lattice of dyons that have trivial mutual braiding in an R^N gauge theory. This condensation is implemented microscopically by gauging a non-on-site 1-form symmetry of the R^N toric code.

entry.title: CCZ gate without strong Rydberg blockade
entry.summary: CCZ gate beyond the strong Rydberg-blockade regime arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes a protocol for a controlled-controlled-Z (CCZ) quantum gate on a neutral-atom platform, using three individually addressable atoms in an optical tweezer array with finite Rydberg interactions. It achieves the conditional phase through successive Rydberg excitation and analytically determined pulses. Numerical comparisons with a fast Rydberg-antiblockade-based protocol show better gate performance at larger interatomic separations within the parameter range considered.

entry.title: Reliability of quantum communication over quantum erasure channels
entry.summary: Reliability of quantum communication over erasure channels arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how fast the error probability of sending quantum information over erasure channels can decay as the number of channel uses grows, for rates below the quantum capacity. This optimal exponential decay rate is the reliability function. For erasure channels with prime input dimension, the authors determine this function exactly at all positive rates below capacity that meet or exceed an explicit critical rate. They show that stabilizer coding strategies achieve this optimal reliability across that range.

entry.title: Odd-even effects on Liouvillian spectra and relaxation in boundary-driven spin chains
entry.summary: Odd-Even Effects on Liouvillian Spectra and Relaxation Dynamics in Boundary-Driven Spin Chains arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how the parity of chain length affects Liouvillian spectra and relaxation dynamics in boundary-driven XY and cluster spin chains. With bulk couplings and boundary dissipation fixed, odd- and even-length chains behave qualitatively differently, with only some chains supporting non-decaying oscillatory modes. The authors attribute this to coupling between bulk Majorana paths and boundary jump operators. The mechanism is said to extend to even-range cluster interactions.

entry.title: Faster Simulation of Quantum Error Correction Under Coherent Noise Using Compiled Tensor Networks
entry.summary: Accelerating Quantum Error Correction Simulations under Coherent Noise with Compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product States arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product State (CAMPS) framework for simulating quantum error correction under coherent noise. It reuses Clifford transformations across measurement shots, recycles qubits released by measurements, and speeds up sampling through rotation fusion and compilation suited to the MPS layout. Benchmarks on surface codes and the [[72,12,6]] bivariate bicycle code show that compiled CAMPS converges at smaller bond dimensions than the uncompiled version and reaches order-of-magnitude sampling speedups at equal bond dimension.

entry.title: Identifying conserved quantum sectors from measurement record statistics
entry.summary: Distinguishing Conserved Quantum Sectors via Measurement Record Features arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a method for identifying conserved sectors of a quantum system by repeatedly measuring an ancillary probe. The method uses a feature vector built from the average outcome frequency and pair-outcome correlations up to K measurement cycles apart, costing time linear in record length for fixed K. In quantum non-demolition measurement models, the average outcome frequency alone gives accurate identification. For an interacting spin bath with nontrivial dynamics within each sector, including temporal correlations substantially improves classification fidelity.

entry.title: Topological Quantum Reservoir Computing: A Method That Stores Temporal Information in Protected Edge States
entry.summary: Topological Quantum Reservoir Computing arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes topological quantum reservoir computing, which uses protected degrees of freedom for storage and the host system's intrinsic bulk dynamics for information processing. Using a one-dimensional Kitaev chain, it shows that long-lived Majorana edge modes and fast bulk responses can support these two functions within the same many-body system. The authors report improved performance on tasks requiring long-term retention of temporal information, and suggest a route toward near-term quantum computing and quantum machine learning.

entry.title: Fast Spectra and Dynamics Method Using Tangent-Space Chebyshev Tree Tensor Networks
entry.summary: Efficient Spectra and Dynamics with Tangent-Space Chebyshev Tree Tensor Networks arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper introduces the tangent-space Chebyshev method (TaChe), which combines tree tensor network states, Chebyshev recursion, and maximum entropy spectral analysis within the tangent space of a tree tensor network to compute quantum many-body spectra and dynamics. Implemented on a GPU, it reports speedups of up to 46.8 over the previous Chebyshev tensor network method and 13.7 over one-site time-dependent variational principle propagation. Applications include acetonitrile, thermal aggregate emission, finite-temperature charge transport on a 6×6 lattice, and internal conversion in aggregates of up to 100 molecules.

entry.title: Quantum Mpemba effect in a driven-dissipative atom-waveguide system
entry.summary: Quantum Mpemba effect in a driven-dissipative atom-waveguide coupled system arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect, where a more strongly disturbed quantum system returns to its steady state faster than a less disturbed one, in a weakly driven and dissipative atomic array coupled to a one-dimensional chiral waveguide. The authors reset one atom to its ground state as a local quench and track the relaxation afterward. Quenching atoms near the array edges speeds up early relaxation through stronger coupling to superradiant modes, and strong directional decay concentrates these modes near one boundary. Later relaxation is dominated by long-lived subradiant modes in the bulk. Coupling two arrays with different spacings also produces an interface-induced effect.

entry.title: Analysis of a homodyne-like scheme using photon counters and a weak local oscillator
entry.summary: Analysis of a Homodyne-Like Measurement Scheme Using Photon Counters and Weak Local Oscillator arXiv · Nov 18, 2026Standard homodyne detection mixes an unknown light signal with a strong local oscillator at a beam splitter to measure a quadrature. This paper studies a variant that uses photon-counting detectors and a weak local oscillator, keeping its mode fixed while varying phase and intensity. It examines which features of the unknown state can be inferred from total photon counts on one or both outputs, in the infinite-data limit.

entry.title: Parity operator spectrum for parafermions and parabosons via character formulas
entry.summary: Spectrum of the parity operator for parafermions and parabosons from character formulas arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper computes the spectrum of the parity operator P for parafermions and parabosons, which are particle-statistics models in quantum theory, using character formulas instead of direct operator action. For n parafermions, the action of P is derived from so(2n+2) character formulas. For n parabosons, the known spectrum of P yields new character formulas for certain osp(2|2n) representations.

entry.title: A quantum algorithm for Exact Cover 3 that beats Grover's square-root speed
entry.summary: Faster than square-root run-time in adiabatic quantum algorithms for Exact Cover 3 arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper combines ideas from sequential and adiabatic quantum computing to propose a quantum algorithm for Exact Cover 3, a sub-class of 3-SAT problems that is NP-complete. The authors report a run-time significantly faster than the square-root N→N^{1/2} scaling of Grover's algorithm. Depending on problem structure, such as clause connectivity, the scaling may range from about N^{1/3} to nearly N^{1/4}, possibly even faster.

entry.title: Analysis of second-harmonic generation in quantum-well metasurfaces, with nonlinear current and boundary conditions
entry.summary: Analysis of the Second-Harmonic Generation Process in Nonlinear Metasurfaces Based on Multiple Quantum Wells: The Approach of Nonlinear Current Density, and The Development of Boundary Conditions arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a new method for analyzing second-harmonic generation in metasurfaces built from multiple quantum wells (MQWs). It formulates the nonlinear current density in the MQW region as the source of the second-harmonic wave, including a saturation effect, and defines periodic boundary conditions for the second-harmonic field. These elements are combined into a semi-analytical framework and checked against previously reported experimental data. The authors also design an MQW and plasmonic metasurface for an 8 µm fundamental wavelength, reporting a 0.02% conversion efficiency at an incident intensity of 23.5 kW/cm².

entry.title: Visualizing chiral snake states in a qubit array using programmable synthetic magnetic fields
entry.summary: Imaging chiral snake states in a qubit array with programmable gauge fields arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper digitally simulates the Harper-Hofstadter model on a 49-qubit superconducting processor with programmable synthetic magnetic fields. Single-qubit Z rotations set the flux of all 36 plaquettes independently, revealing Aharonov-Bohm suppression, disorder-induced slowing and magnetic reflection. At a field reversal, bonding and antibonding initial states propagate in opposite directions, and both reverse when the field is inverted. A symmetry analysis yields a chiral displacement of nearly one lattice spacing after ten Trotter rounds.

entry.title: Aharonov-Bohm blockade of full field reversal in coupled Rabi cavities
entry.summary: Aharonov-Bohm blockade of complete reversal in coupled Rabi cavities arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how two bistable light fields in a pair of coupled quantum Rabi cavities reverse under a shared bias. Near half a flux quantum, the two routes to full reversal interfere destructively, blocking the last step: under a slow sweep, only one field reverses with probability 0.998, even though the final bias favors reversing both. A four-state model describes how the width of this blockade window narrows with sweep time.

entry.title: Comment on a paper about eigenvalues of the toroidal dipole operator
entry.summary: Comment on "The eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the toroidal dipole operator' arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This comment shows that the spectrum of the operator T̂₃⁽ᶿ⁾ studied by Anghel and Dolineanu (Phys. Scr. 2023) is continuous rather than discrete, contrary to the original authors' claim. It concludes that no experimentally observable splitting of energy levels corresponds to this operator.

entry.title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts: a trainability-friendly approach to hybrid quantum-classical learning
entry.summary: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes Soft-MoQE, a Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts architecture that replaces variational quantum training with input-dependent selection and combination of fixed quantum feature maps. It consists of a pool of non-trainable quantum circuits, each defining a distinct embedding, and a classical gating network that weights these embeddings for each data point. Benchmarked on three PCA-reduced tasks, Soft-MoQE outperforms the single best expert, the uniform average of experts, and a linear baseline, reaching performance comparable to a trainable quantum neural network without optimizing any quantum parameters.

entry.title: Efficient Simulation of Variational Quantum Circuits on CPUs and GPUs
entry.summary: Efficient simulation of variational quantum circuits: representation, accuracy and CPU/GPU allocation arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper compares several methods for classically simulating variational quantum circuits on CPU and GPU systems, including gate-based statevector simulation, direct Pauli evolution, and matrix product states. It tests molecular and spin Variational Hamiltonian Ansatze as well as hardware-efficient ansatze, varying circuit width, depth, precision, and resource allocation. The authors also provide a procedure for jointly choosing the representation, precision, and worker allocation based on the cost of complete energy evaluations.

entry.title: Beyond Corpus Imitation: Musical Mindsets Evolving via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Beyond Corpus-Driven Imitation: Evolving Musical Mindsets in the Agentic Orchestra via Quantum Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a framework for computer-aided music composition and performance called the agentic orchestra, in which quantum-circuit-based musical agents evolve distinct mindsets through trial-and-error interaction with a musical environment rather than training on large datasets. Two agent architectures are described: atomistic agents that process pitch and rhythm independently, and holistic agents that treat pitch and duration as unified note events. Mindsets are shaped by musically grounded reward functions that can be combined and weighted. Experiments on IBM quantum hardware indicate that musically meaningful learning is achievable with existing quantum computers.

entry.title: Quantum annealing with a quantum neural network: why network width matters
entry.summary: Quantum Annealing with a Quantum Neural Network: Width of Annealing Matters arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper extends quantum annealing into a quantum neural network and evaluates its performance on several prototypical optimization problems. The authors report that a random quantum annealing network of width W = 2 can exponentially reduce the number of evolution layers, or depth, needed in a quantum search problem. By tuning network parameters, a quantum perceptron of depth L = 1 and width W = 2 can solve the search problem with exponentially small errors. The authors conclude that network width provides a larger, learnable evolution space that raises the algorithm's success probability.

entry.title: S and Double-Exponential Transformations with Moment Expansion for Three-Centre Coulomb and Hybrid Integrals
entry.summary: The S and Double-Exponential Transformations with a Moment Expansion for Three-Centre Coulomb and Hybrid Integrals arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies numerical evaluation of three-centre two-electron Coulomb and hybrid integrals over exponential-type functions, which contain oscillatory spherical Bessel functions. It combines the S transformation with Fourier-type double-exponential quadrature, which needs substantially fewer quadrature nodes for high accuracy than direct double-exponential quadrature. The authors also identify a geometry-dependent oscillation-to-damping ratio and build a convergent moment expansion for the weakly oscillatory regime. The method is tested on H2O and C2H4 molecular integrals over Slater-type functions.

entry.title: Spatial cost of recovering a fusion qubit in a critical spin chain.
entry.summary: Geometric limits of quantum recovery across an Ising transition arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how much physical space is needed to recover a fusion qubit with vanishing error from a fixed-sector ground doublet of four Kramers–Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain. To leading order, the required span of physical spins is at least that of the shorter three-defect interval. An exact interval decoder is shown to attain this bound, and successful near-minimal supports concentrate on the shortest interval at leading order.

entry.title: Estimating ground-state energy on cat qubits: FeMoco-54 in 23.5 hours with 7,164 qubits
entry.summary: Ground-state energy estimation compiled on cat qubits: 6 808 qubits for FeMoco-54 in 23.6 hours arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a detailed resource estimate for the sum-of-squares block encoding algorithm of Low et al. applied to electronic structure Hamiltonians, compiled for superconducting cat qubits. It gives closed-form costs for key subroutines and global layouts for repetition-cat and LDPC-cat architectures, combined with adder compilation from a companion work. Under stated assumptions, the authors report that FeMoco-54 needs fewer than 7,500 cat qubits with an expected runtime under one day per phase estimation run on the LDPC-cat architecture.

entry.title: Quantum entanglement and parametric resonance in coupled oscillators
entry.summary: Runaway entanglement between a semiclassical background and parametrically-enhanced quantum fluctuations arXiv · Oct 12, 2026This paper studies two quadratically coupled harmonic oscillators, one in the ground state and one in a coherent state, as a toy model for a quantum field mode in an oscillating classical background. Using the Feynman-Vernon influence functional, the authors perturbatively compute the purity of the mixed state obtained by tracing out one oscillator. They find runaway growth of entanglement between the oscillators and rapid breakdown of perturbation theory in regions of parametric instability.

entry.title: Singlet flags restore circuit distance of shuttled quantum LDPC codes in silicon
entry.summary: Singlet flags: using native entanglement to restore the circuit distance of shuttled qLDPC codes in silicon arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper addresses measuring high-weight checks of quantum LDPC codes on silicon spin-qubit processors by shuttling an ancilla electron. The authors make the ancilla half of a spin singlet whose partner stays home, and use a Bell measurement at the end of each check as a flag for isolated bit-flip faults during the walk. Tests on new distance-6 codes and circuit-level simulations show that the flag restores circuit distance and lowers logical error rates across several code families. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use a spin-singlet partner as a flag to restore circuit distance of shuttled qLDPC codes, with exact distance solvers and circuit-level simulations reported.

entry.title: QCCDCert: A formally verified compiler for co-designing QCCD trapped-ion quantum hardware and software
entry.summary: QCCDCert: Formally Verified Compilation for QCCD Co-Design arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper presents a co-design framework built on a compiler verified in the Lean language, for comparing trapped-ion QCCD quantum computers with different trap sizes and layouts. Hardware descriptions and operating rules are treated as compiler inputs, so one theorem covers every candidate design. On 75 benchmark programs of 11 to 130 qubits, the best design found reduced modeled execution time by 66% on average compared with the worst design of equal capacity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply a Lean-verified compiler to QCCD co-design, proving one theorem across designs. They report 75 benchmarks and 11 defects in three prior compilers.

entry.title: Scrambling as the source of entanglement cost in non-local quantum computation
entry.summary: Scrambling leads to entanglement cost in NLQC arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies the entanglement needed to implement a joint quantum channel in non-local quantum computation (NLQC). The authors introduce a new lower-bound technique based on scrambling, showing that a unitary has zero entanglement cost exactly when it does not scramble. They further show that the tripartite mutual information, which measures scrambling, gives a quantitative lower bound on NLQC entanglement cost. Using this bound, they also prove that controllable correlation is a faithful lower bound, resolving a conjecture of Cleve and May. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link scrambling to NLQC entanglement cost, give a faithful lower bound, and report resolving a Cleve-May conjecture.

entry.title: Covering Pauli Observables: Sampling Thresholds and Design Effect of Measurement Settings
entry.summary: Covering the Pauli Observables: Sampling Thresholds and the Design Effect of a Measurement Setting arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies how many random measurement settings are needed to cover a given fraction of all Pauli observables, where each setting assigns X, Y, or Z to every qubit and one run estimates all observables it covers. It shows that the covered fraction has a sharp threshold at a growth rate of 3^(3/4) per qubit and gives an explicit expression for the number of settings needed, with random sampling asymptotically optimal up to a factor below 1.69. The authors also define a design effect for each setting that captures correlations among estimates, and in six-qubit simulations report 7.6 to 38 times fewer circuit runs than measuring observables independently. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link Pauli observable covering to rate-distortion theory, giving a 3^{3/4} threshold and near-optimal random sampling, plus a closed-form mean design effect verified in six-qubit simulatio

entry.title: Individually addressable CCZ gates on near-good quantum LDPC codes, and near-optimal magic state protocols
entry.summary: Addressable transversal CCZ gates on almost good quantum LDPC codes and nearly optimal magic state protocols arXiv · Nov 18, 2026Under a uniform subfield product expansion assumption, the paper constructs quantum LDPC codes with distance Ω_ε(N/log²N) that support at least N^{1-ε} individually addressable logical CCZ gates. The codes are built as balanced products of expanding graph covers. Applications include CCZ distillation with arbitrarily small overhead exponent and a magic state fountain that prepares many encoded CCZ states. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct qLDPC codes with addressable transversal CCZ gates and near-optimal magic state protocols, relying on a subfield product expansion assumption, reporting distance and gate-count b

entry.title: Separating QMA from QCMA via a classical oracle and a polynomial switching lemma
entry.summary: Separating QMA from the QCMA Hierarchy via a Switching Lemma for Polynomials arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper constructs a classical oracle relative to which QMA is not contained in the QCMA hierarchy. Its main tool is a switching lemma for bounded polynomials, whose parameters do not depend on the number of input variables. The authors also build two further oracles: one where QCMA collapses to P but QMA does not, and one where QMA collapses to P but PP does not. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a polynomial switching lemma giving a new viewpoint on a QMA versus QCMA oracle separation, plus two further collapse separations.

entry.title: Compute Before Digitizing: ADC-less Mixed-Signal Readout for Cryogenic Qubits
entry.summary: Compute Before You Digitize: ADC-less Mixed-Signal Processing for Scalable Cryogenic Qubit Readout arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents DIRAC, an in-cryostat qubit readout architecture that removes Nyquist-rate analog-to-digital converters by performing demodulation and averaging in the analog domain. Passive complex mixers, ping-pong active-RC integrators, and a time-domain digitizing stage process the front-end output before conversion. Designed in 22 nm FD-SOI and evaluated at 4 K on 1.12M experimental shots, it matches the fidelity of an FP32 digital pipeline while using far less energy. It also reduces 4 K power per physical qubit by 50.4% relative to a fixed-point pipeline. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose ADC-less cryogenic qubit readout using analog computation; they report FP32-matching fidelity on 1.12M shots and energy and logical-error comparisons.

entry.title: Optimal joint bounds for estimating and preparing sparse quantum ground states
entry.summary: Optimal Joint Bounds for Sparse Ground-State Energy Estimation and Ground-State Preparation arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies the quantum query complexity of ground-state energy estimation and ground-state preparation for sparse Hamiltonians. It proves lower bounds that scale with the square root of the sparsity, the overlap, the error, and the gap, even for stoquastic Hamiltonians. The authors also provide matching upper-bound algorithms in a reversible in-place sparse-location model. These results show that the square-root dependence on sparsity is both necessary and sufficient. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give matching sparse-query lower and upper bounds for GSEE and GSP, jointly in sparsity s, overlap, precision and failure probability.

entry.title: Stationary quantum time series: spectral theory of memory in measured processes
entry.summary: Stationary Quantum Time Series: Spectral Theory of Process Memory and Measurement Records arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper extends classical time series concepts such as stationarity, ergodicity, and spectral representation to time series produced by quantum experiments. The authors develop a process-tensor framework and establish structural theorems for stationary processes of finite quantum Markov order. The results are presented as a foundation for quantum spectral analysis, model identification, and single-trajectory inference.

entry.title: Critical-localized reentry under periodic spacer control
entry.summary: Critical--localized reentry under periodic spacer control arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies a fixed fraction of a quasiperiodic spectrum in a matched-dimer chain, varying only the spacer on-site energies to observe repeated alternation between critical and localized behavior. An exact Bloch-determinant identity links the physical spectrum to the bands of a periodic reference operator. For the golden cell frequency, the authors prove that the spectrum inside the open reference bands is critical, while the spectrum outside them is pure point with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions.

entry.title: Controlling charge localization and work reliability in collective quantum batteries by tuning reservoir spectra
entry.summary: Spectral Engineering of Charge Localization and Work Reliability in Collective Quantum Batteries arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies an interacting collective-spin quantum battery in which engineering the reservoir spectrum controls where excitation accumulates and how reliably work can be extracted. Analytical results link the pump-to-loss ratio to charge localization, fluctuations, and extractable work. The authors show that reservoirs with the same mean charge can produce different localization and charging times.

entry.title: QWeaver: A Workflow for Cutting Quantum Circuits with Compiler, Runtime, and Classical Recombination
entry.summary: QWeaver: Quantum Circuit Cut Workflow with MLIR-based Compiler, Runtime, and Weaver Hybrid Tasks arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper presents QWeaver, a framework that orchestrates quantum circuit cutting, which splits a large OpenQASM circuit into smaller subcircuits that can run on limited quantum hardware. It builds a task graph in which an MLIR-based cut task creates fragments, execution tasks run them concurrently across backends via the Q-IRIS runtime, and a weaving task recombines the results using quasi-probability reconstruction. The authors validate end-to-end reconstruction on GHZ and Harris-Ross instances and evaluate system and width trade-offs on structured GHZ simulator workloads.

entry.title: Measuring subsystem evolution with a quantum clock in the history state formalism
entry.summary: Subsystem evolution in the history state formalism arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper introduces a relational framework for describing how parts of a quantum system evolve relative to a quantum reference clock, using correlations in a history state. It defines a subsystem-clock mutual information to quantify the evolution of open subsystems, which can be non-unitary. The authors derive analytical expressions for qubit clocks and illustrate the results with spin-1/2 and spin-1 quantum walks.

entry.title: Post-selection method for quantum LDPC codes using parity pushes to reject unreliable shots
entry.summary: Parity Push Post-Selection with Soft Parity Constraints for Quantum LDPC Codes arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes PPPS (parity push post-selection), a decoder-agnostic method for quantum low-density parity-check codes. For each logical observable, the shot is re-decoded with a push toward the opposite parity, and it is accepted only if every re-decoding stays in the original logical class. With degenerate maximum-likelihood decoding, a shot is accepted exactly when the logical gap exceeds the push strength. Simulations on specific bivariate bicycle codes show the logical error rate is substantially reduced at rejection rates near 1%.

entry.title: Low-loss tunable coupled-mode Hamiltonian in tripartite van der Waals cavity magnonics
entry.summary: Hierarchical coupling in tripartite van der Waals cavity magnonics for a low-loss and tunable coupled-mode Hamiltonian arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies a tripartite van der Waals cavity magnonic system built from CrCl3. It realizes a hierarchical anti-crossing structure that yields an effective coupled-dual-mode Hamiltonian. The authors report an order-of-magnitude reduction in loss while keeping strong coupling. They also theoretically show that loss and coupling can be tuned simultaneously by changing the magnetic field direction and strength. The device is micrometer-thick and a few millimeters wide, much smaller than bulk-crystal-based designs.

entry.title: Chirped-pulse charging for stable two-level quantum batteries
entry.summary: Chirp-stabilized charging of a two-level quantum battery arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies charging a two-level quantum battery with chirped pulses, which avoids the pulse-area dependence and energy backflow of resonant Rabi driving. The authors compare four pairings of sech or Gaussian envelopes with linear or tanh frequency sweeps. They report that strong chirp converts charging into adiabatic rapid passage, yielding stored energy and ergotropy plateaus that are nearly insensitive to pulse area, with the sech-tanh combination performing best.

entry.title: Renormalization and exact Bloch bands in the trigonometric Rosen-Morse model
entry.summary: Renormalization and exact Bloch bands: the trigonometric Rosen-Morse model arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies the trigonometric Rosen-Morse potential both as an isolated singular well and as an exactly solvable periodic lattice. The potential combines inverse-square singularities with Coulomb terms of opposite signs. In the strongly attractive regime, independent renormalization at the two endpoints yields a two-parameter family of spectra. The authors derive the exact Bloch dispersion relation for the weak-medium regime, where self-adjoint matching conditions allow transmission between neighboring cells, and determine band widths, gaps, and effective masses.

entry.title: Parisi energy emerges before Parisi geometry in QAOA on spin glasses
entry.summary: Parisi Energy before Parisi Geometry in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) behaves on spin glass problems, treating its output distribution as a statistical-physics object probed in the thermodynamic limit. Typical samples remain macroscopically uncorrelated, while the low-energy tail shows stronger overlap and a Parisi-like phase with the same critical behavior as the thermal spin-glass transition. As circuit depth increases, the onset of this organization moves toward the typical output.

entry.title: Extreme-value statistics for majorisation partial orders
entry.summary: Extreme value statistics for majorisation partial orders arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies extreme-value behaviour of random samples in partially ordered sets, examining their meets and joins as order-theoretic analogues of minima and maxima. The authors consider the probability simplex equipped with either UT-majorisation or majorisation, with samples drawn uniformly from the corresponding simplex. They analyse these extrema both for fixed dimension and as the dimension grows, showing almost-sure collapse to bottom or top elements and identifying critical scalings with nondegenerate limiting laws.

entry.title: Uniformly convergent perturbation theory for open quantum systems near exceptional points
entry.summary: Uniformly Convergent Perturbation Theory for Open Quantum Systems at, near, and away from Exceptional Points arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies perturbation theory for open quantum systems near Liouvillian exceptional points, where standard spectral perturbation theory becomes ill-conditioned. Using a Dyson expansion that avoids diagonalizing the perturbed generator, the authors analyze the scaling, stability and convergence of perturbative corrections. They provide a uniform-in-time error estimate valid for any relaxing finite-dimensional Lindbladian, and test it on a driven two-level system.

entry.title: Quantum algorithms for hidden subgroups in unitriangular groups
entry.summary: Perspectives on the hidden subgroup problem over unitriangular groups arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies the quantum Hidden Subgroup Problem over upper unitriangular groups U_n(F_p). It first analyzes U_4(F_p), the smallest such group with nilpotency class three, and shows the limits of the Pretty Good Measurement approach used for Heisenberg groups. It then adapts existing techniques to the general U_n(F_p) and derives an algorithm for cyclic subgroups, which is not efficient in the group size.

entry.title: Instrument indeterminacy: how uncertainty in quantum measurement effects can be separated and read in neutrosophic terms
entry.summary: Instrument indeterminacy: separating uncertainty in POVM effects and its neutrosophic reading arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper addresses the open question of how indeterminacy in neutrosophic annotations of quantum measurements can be defined operationally. It shows that this indeterminacy cannot be obtained from outcome probabilities alone but can be computed from the state and effect together, giving an explicit formula for binary POVMs. The authors link it to a total-variance decomposition and an estimator that, in simulation, needs 2.5 to 6 times fewer shots than detector tomography.

entry.title: Spectral disks bounding quantum Markov generators
entry.summary: Spectral Disks for Quantum Markov Generators arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies spectral bounds for quantum Markov generators in GKLS form. The authors prove that the spectrum of a generator written without a Hamiltonian lies in a disk tangent to the imaginary axis, with radius given by the norm of an operator built from the jump map. They also show that a conjecture relating the escape rate to the spectral disk fails for a qutrit with a single normal jump.

entry.title: Fe²⁺:forsterite qubit system: a proposed iron-ion-based quantum bit design
entry.summary: Fe²⁺:forsterite Qubit System arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This study proposes a qubit system based on Fe²⁺ ions in forsterite. The authors solve the unitary time evolution of the quantum state vector under the system's Hamiltonian, using known axial and transverse anisotropy terms, at temperatures up to 10 K. They report that population can be transferred between the two lowest states at Rabi half-period rates with 99.9% fidelity, and held at a desired state without decoherence. The results are said to hold up to 10 K.

entry.title: Quantum resources and the Monte Carlo sign problem
entry.summary: Quantum resources and the onset of the quantum Monte Carlo sign problem arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how the Monte Carlo sign problem, a barrier to simulating quantum many-body systems, relates to quantum resources. The authors tune the nonstoquasticity of random k-local Hamiltonians and use tensor-network calculations to track entanglement and nonstabilizerness of the ground state. They find that quantum Monte Carlo simulations deteriorate in the region where these resources sharply increase, and they support this with analytic constructions and results on graph states.

entry.title: Trade-off between polynomial degree and normalization in bounded QSVT matrix inversion
entry.summary: Degree and normalization frontiers for bounded QSVT inversion arXiv · Nov 18, 2026Quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) performs matrix inversion using bounded polynomials. The paper analyzes how increasing polynomial degree improves normalization and reduces amplified query cost, for two error criteria: absolute reciprocal error and residual error. For absolute reciprocal error, it establishes a scaling limit to a constrained least-norm problem for entire functions and characterizes the high-accuracy frontier using elliptic integrals. For residual error, a sparse Chebyshev construction is presented, and both achieve certified query-cost savings over minimax baselines.

entry.title: Quantum optimal transport in spacetime using spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and states
entry.summary: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper extends optimal transport theory to spacetime by proposing a quantum optimal transport problem formulated with spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions and spatiotemporal states. The authors show that these two formalisms are equivalent and related through spatiotemporal operator frames. The work gives rigorous definitions and a discussion of duality, and introduces a spatiotemporal quantum Wasserstein metric that satisfies the metric axioms.

entry.title: High-rate, low-distance color codes for encoding multiple logical qubits
entry.summary: High-rate low-distance color codes arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes small two-dimensional color codes with high encoding rates for encoding multiple logical qubits, including distance-3 codes with rates up to 1/3 and distance-4 codes with rates up to 1/4. The authors prove these rates are optimal for color codes with only color boundaries on surfaces with non-negative Euler characteristic. Simulations of Steane-style error correction with real-time feedback and no post-selection in an all-to-all connected linear trapped-ion chain show that the codes [[20,4,4]] and [[16,4,4]] reach break-even at two-qubit gate infidelities of 0.22% and 0.26%. Their performance matches that of Shor-style error correction with bivariate bicycle codes using weight-5 measurements.

entry.title: Experimental limits on gauge hidden-variable models in Bell tests
entry.summary: Experimental constraints on gauge hidden-variable models in Bell tests arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper tests whether measurements realizing the same final effect give identical statistics, using polarization-entangled photons with a setting implemented either directly or via closed wave-plate loops. The authors develop a local path-memory model and derive a mixed-context Bell bound. The direct implementation violates the Bell inequality, while the looped mixed-context results are indistinguishable from it within experimental precision, constraining path-sensitive hidden-variable extensions.

entry.title: Simulating molecular twisting during light-driven molecular switching on hybrid quantum hardware
entry.summary: Qubit-qumode simulation of molecular torsion in photoisomerization arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes a hybrid quantum simulation framework that combines qubits and continuous-variable qumodes to model photochemical reactions such as retinal photoisomerization. Electronic states are mapped to qubits, vibrations to qumodes, and periodic molecular torsion to a compact qumode encoding. Numerical results show that accounting for the circular topology of torsion can significantly change the calculated observables. The authors also introduce two methods to reduce the hardware resources needed for these encodings.

entry.title: Symmetry classification of molecular rovibrational states and entangled carrier states
entry.summary: Symmetry classification of hyperfine rovibrational molecular phase space arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper builds a phase space theory of molecules by jointly treating rotational, vibrational, and nuclear-spin degrees of freedom as a quotient by the point group. Molecular states are grouped into species according to how these degrees of freedom transform under symmetry. Each species is defined by an absolutely maximally entangled carrier state, or a two-dimensional space of them for 45 species. An example experimental protocol for preparing and driving symmetry-adapted bend states of CaOCH3 is also proposed.

entry.title: Collective superconducting-qubit interfaces for converting microwave quantum signals to optical ones
entry.summary: Collective Superconducting-Qubit Interfaces for Microwave-to-Optical Quantum Transduction arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies a transducer in which many superconducting qubits couple together to one shared optomechanical resonator, converting microwave quantum signals into optical ones. The authors find that qubit count and optical pump strength together set conversion efficiency, added noise, and bandwidth. In a lossless four-qubit benchmark, adding mechanical anharmonicity raises the final single-photon target probability from 19.6% to 99.7%. Pair-dependent qubit interactions are reported to lower optical retrieval efficiency from 58% to 35%.

entry.title: Preparing Quantum States Without Time-Varying Control
entry.summary: Look Mum, No Hands! Quantum State Preparation without Time-Dependent Control arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies which quantum states can be prepared by a system whose time-invariant Hamiltonian cannot be modulated, so control relies only on fixed coupling strengths and evolution time. It characterizes the autonomously reachable set and introduces two unreachability criteria, one cheap and rigorous, the other based on exhaustive numerical optimization. For sufficiently random control terms and long enough evolution times, almost every state becomes approximately reachable, approaching the expressivity of time-dependent control at the cost of longer evolution.

entry.title: Steerability of top quark pairs in LHC decays
entry.summary: Steerability in top quark decays at the LHC arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) steerability in top quark pairs produced at the Large Hadron Collider, a property lying between entanglement and Bell nonlocality. The authors use both decay and kinematic methods to estimate the sensitivity of the LHC and High Luminosity LHC to detect steerable states. They report significances and measurement precisions across channels and kinematic regions, and discuss the interpretation of these results.

entry.title: Scanned electron probe for efficient Zernike phase-contrast imaging
entry.summary: Zernike-efficient phase contrast with a scanned electron probe arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes APEX, a scanned-probe imaging mode that combines a defocused probe, a π/2 phase element in a magnified probe crossover image, and in-focus detection at each scan position. In a linear model of a weak-phase object, APEX transfers nearly all Zernike Fisher information over a wide band. Idealized simulations show more accurate phase reconstruction than defocused 4D-STEM ptychography, and a single scan can separate two phase screens 150 nm apart at known depths.

entry.title: Expressive power of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states
entry.summary: Expressivity of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies exact tensor network representations of two-dimensional translation-invariant Gaussian fermionic states, covering single-band BCS superconductors and half-filled two-band insulators (including semimetals). For both families, the authors prove that an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy is equivalent to the existence of an exact Gaussian fermionic tensor network state with a finite bond dimension set by that entropy. The paper also gives equivalent characterizations based on compactly supported Wannier-type orbitals and the momentum-space wavefunction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that a Rényi-0 area law is equivalent to an exact Gaussian fermionic tensor network representation with finite bond dimension in 2D.

entry.title: A mathematical proof that certain electron-photon ground-state quantities determine the external potentials
entry.summary: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper proves a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of electron configuration with values in spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in L^6 locally, and the divergence, curl and scalar potential in L^p locally for some p>2. As an application, it proves a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove unique continuation for Pauli-Fierz eigenstates under weak regularity and derive a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling.

entry.title: Entanglement cost and classical capacity of multimode Gaussian states and channels
entry.summary: Entanglement cost and classical capacity of multimode Gaussian states and channels arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies the entanglement cost and classical capacity of multimode Gaussian states and channels in continuous-variable quantum information. The authors prove that entanglement of formation, Gaussian entanglement of formation, and entanglement cost coincide for finite-energy bipartite Gaussian states, and that this value lower-bounds these quantities for non-Gaussian states with the same covariance matrix. They determine the entanglement cost and the energy-constrained classical capacity of every multimode Gaussian channel, both reducing to Gaussian covariance optimizations. The capacity is achieved by pure Gaussian signals with Gaussian displacement modulation. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove equality of three entanglement measures for Gaussian states and determine multimode Gaussian channel capacity and entanglement cost via proofs.

entry.title: Catalytic imaginarity transformations: using an unconsumed auxiliary system to make otherwise impossible quantum state conversions possible with real operations
entry.summary: Catalytic imaginarity transformations arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies catalytic state transformations in the resource theory of imaginarity, a property of quantum states. A catalyst with imaginarity enables conversions that are impossible using only real operations, without being consumed. The authors analyze deterministic conversion, stochastic-approximate conversion, and the effects of catalyst recovery and multiple rounds on the success probability. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show a maximally imaginary pure state is the unique deterministic catalyst and derive optimal stochastic-approximate catalytic success probabilities and tradeoffs, limited to imaginarity t

entry.title: Proving LABS optimality with a quantum-classical branch and bound method
entry.summary: Proven optimality for LABS with quantum-classical branch and bound arXiv · Nov 17, 2026Low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) are used as radar phase codes and digital communication sync words. The paper presents a quantum-classical branch and bound algorithm in which fixed-angle QAOA samples the Hamiltonians of search-tree nodes to supply candidate sequences and branching choices, while classical bounds prune the tree. The method either proves optimality or, if stopped early, returns the best sequence found with a certified lower bound and gap. The authors report proven optima for lengths 2 to 30 and explicitly claim no speedup. ★★★★ Notable: The authors embed fixed-angle QAOA in branch and bound to prove LABS optimality, reporting proven optima for lengths 2 to 30 and bound trajectories over time, without claiming speedup.

entry.title: Minimum Measurement Rounds for Perfect Encoded Fusion
entry.summary: Optimal Measurement Rounds for Perfect Encoded Fusion arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies encoded fusion, where probabilistic physical fusions implement a logical Bell measurement, and determines the minimum worst-case number of measurement rounds needed to perfectly fuse two blocks of an irreducible [[n,1]] stabilizer code. In a lossless model, the optimum equals the minimum root eccentricity over the local complementation orbit of graphs representing the code, and the lower bound holds for any adaptive perfect strategy. The paper also gives a matching strategy and characterizes the batch sequences possible on all-failure branches via a graph adjacency condition. ★★★★ Notable: The authors determine the optimal worst-case measurement rounds for perfect encoded fusion, matching a minimum root eccentricity bound with a constructive strategy.

entry.title: Strong eigenstate thermalization in Singer-cycle Clifford circuits
