entry.summary: Strong eigenstate thermalization in Singer-cycle Clifford circuits arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, a framework for how isolated quantum systems thermalize. It introduces brickwork Clifford circuits whose Pauli transformations follow a Singer cycle over F2. The authors prove that all Floquet eigenstates of these circuits are thermal at infinite temperature without exceptions, and they derive uniform bounds on deviations of observables. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that all Floquet eigenstates of Singer-cycle Clifford circuits thermalize at infinite temperature without exceptions, with uniform bounds.

entry.title: Complex mobility edges from competing localization channels in non-Hermitian quasicrystals
entry.summary: Complex mobility edges from competing localization channels in non-Hermitian quasicrystals arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper extends the Ganeshan-Pixley-Das Sarma model with asymmetric hopping and complex onsite potential to describe a broad class of non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains. Using Avila's global theory, the authors derive exact Lyapunov exponents, find thresholds of two localization channels on the complex-energy plane, and propose a selection rule separating physical mobility edges from suppressed candidates. The channel controlling localization can switch with energy, producing complex mobility edges of non-Hermitian origin, and nonreciprocal hopping shifts these thresholds and the bulk spectrum. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce competing localization channels in non-Hermitian quasicrystals, derive exact Lyapunov exponents via Avila's global theory, and report numerical verification of the complex mobili

entry.title: Entanglement Lower Bounds for Symmetric Quantum Circuits: A theory paper on what symmetric quantum circuits can compute under entanglement limits
entry.summary: Entanglement Lower Bounds for Symmetric Quantum Circuits arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper studies a tradeoff between circuit size and entanglement width in symmetric quantum circuits, where every symmetry of the input extends to an automorphism of the circuit. It introduces a new quantum pebble game based on the partial trace and shows that a certain graph property, decidable in classical polynomial time, cannot be computed by polynomial-size symmetric quantum circuits with entanglement width o(n/log n). Without entanglement restrictions, the authors show that every graph property in BQP can be computed by such circuits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a new partial-trace quantum pebble game, transferring classical lower bounds to symmetric quantum circuits with restricted entanglement width.

entry.title: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: how crosscap states reveal hidden asymmetry dynamics
entry.summary: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: Asymmetry dynamics of crosscap states arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies how symmetry-breaking coherence encoded in long-range entanglement can become locally accessible under symmetry-preserving unitary dynamics, reversing the usual restoration of local symmetry. It examines a family of charge-deformed crosscap states with antipodal entangled pairs, analyzing their static entanglement and asymmetry. After a quench to a free-fermion tight-binding chain, entanglement entropy decreases while entanglement asymmetry grows, a behavior captured quantitatively by a quasiparticle picture of antipodal correlations.

entry.title: Modeling how quantum information spreads in protein NMR experiments
entry.summary: Modeling quantum information scrambling in realistic protein NMR experiments arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents an end-to-end computational pipeline linking protein molecular structures to out-of-time-order correlator (OTOC) dynamics. It combines molecular dynamics simulations, orientational averaging for powder samples, and spin-network truncation using an experimentally realizable double-quantum effective Hamiltonian. Applied to over 350 carbon-carbon spin pairs across 10 proteins, the authors find that OTOC arrival times scale approximately linearly with interspin distance.

entry.title: Local interference algorithms for computing observables in large random quantum circuits
entry.summary: Local interference algorithms for observables in large random circuits arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how to simulate the evolution of observables in random quantum circuits. The authors show that classical Monte Carlo sampling is not generically defeated by interference effects for first-order out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in unstructured circuits and time-ordered charge-charge correlators (TOCs) in particle-number-preserving circuits. They design algorithms combining Monte Carlo sampling and tensor networks, and numerically observe that computational cost scales polynomially with circuit size and target precision.

entry.title: Performance analysis of a Rydberg atom THz radiometer concept
entry.summary: Performance analysis of a Rydberg atom THz radiometer concept arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines Rydberg atom sensors as an alternative to conventional terahertz receivers, whose technology is less mature than electronics or photonics. The conversion architecture has been shown to coherently transduce thermal radiation at room temperature. The authors assess how feasible such sensors are for THz radiometry in Earth observation.

entry.title: Quantum amplification using a linear quantum coupler (a linear-inductive-coupler-based amplifier for quantum-limited microwave signals)
entry.summary: Quantum amplification with a linear quantum coupler arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies a parametric amplifier built on a linear inductive coupler (LINC) for quantum-limited microwave measurement. The authors derive an effective three-wave-mixing model from the driven-circuit Hamiltonian and analyze gain, saturation, and intermodulation distortion against state-of-the-art designs. They report that the LINC's symmetry-protected structure suppresses static Kerr nonlinearity, and that circuit-parameter optimization further reduces dressed-squeezing and driven-Kerr effects, improving power handling.

entry.title: Teleporting logical qubits between superconducting circuits via lattice surgery
entry.summary: Teleportation of Logical Qubits using Lattice Surgery with Superconducting Circuits arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper experimentally demonstrates teleportation of logical states between two distance-three logical qubits on a superconducting circuit of 41 physical qubits. The method uses lattice surgery, a fault-tolerant operation for surface-code logical qubits. The authors track how logical information moves step by step from source to target qubit. They report that repeating stabilizer measurements after merging two surface-code patches restores fault tolerance and increases the fidelity of the teleported state, with further gains from optimizing gate count and sequence duration.

entry.title: Simulating neutral-meson mixing and decay on a reprogrammable photonic chip
entry.summary: Quantum simulation of neutral-meson mixing and decay on a reprogrammable photonic processor arXiv · Nov 18, 2026Neutral mesons oscillate into their antiparticles while decaying, a process described by a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian that ordinary unitary quantum simulators cannot directly implement. The authors propose a reprogrammable photonic processor that simulates this open-system evolution through dilation and analyze it at the circuit level. Using one fixed device reprogrammed only through control voltages, the simulations reproduce flavor oscillation and decay for neutral kaons and B_d and B_s mesons, and they analyze how unit-to-unit loss variations reduce fidelity.

entry.title: Non-equilibrium topological order in a periodically driven toric code
entry.summary: Non-equilibrium topological order from Floquet anyon proliferation in the toric code arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies the dynamics of Kitaev's toric code under Floquet quenches, where the drive coherently creates and propagates fermionic f anyons. The authors show that the long-time state departs from pure-state topological order yet keeps long-range entanglement, realizing a Floquet analog of intrinsic mixed-state topological order. They derive decompositions of entanglement entropy and logarithmic negativity that separate ground-state contributions, including topological terms, from those of the driven quasiparticles. For non-interacting f dynamics, these decompositions enable free-fermion numerical methods and link the ordered state to f anyons equilibrating to a periodic Gibbs ensemble.

entry.title: Causality, determinism and predictability: how classical and quantum physics view nature differently
entry.summary: Causality, determinism and predictability: Probing nature through classical and quantum eyes arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This article, aimed mainly at students and general readers, examines how our understanding of causality, determinism and predictability changes when moving from classical physics to quantum description. It first explains how determinism and predictability work in classical dynamics and outlines the concept of causality. It then describes how quantum mechanics requires revisiting, and possibly abandoning, these notions, and notes that the role of gravity within the quantum framework remains an open question.

entry.title: Fault-tolerant fusion-based quantum computing with imperfect photon indistinguishability
entry.summary: Performance of Fusion-Based Quantum Computing with Imperfect Photon Indistinguishability arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how imperfect photon indistinguishability affects fault tolerance in fusion-based quantum computing (FBQC). The authors build hardware-motivated noise models and evaluate unencoded and Shor(2,2)-encoded resource states in the 6-ring fusion network, prepared by all-photonic and emitter-assisted repeat-until-success schemes. Encoding lowers the distinguishability threshold from 0.136% to 0.08% for the all-photonic construction, while the RUS construction shows nearly equal thresholds with and without encoding (0.256% and 0.271%). The results indicate that resource-state generation can critically determine the fault tolerance of photonic architectures.

entry.title: Frequency multiplexing of NV centers in a Purcell-enhanced nanocavity
entry.summary: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper integrates multiple nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond into a monolithic photonic crystal nanocavity while keeping near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. Linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz allow spectrally distinct NV centers to be frequency multiplexed within a common cavity mode. Tuning the cavity to the NV zero-phonon line enhances emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations.

entry.title: PRISM: A Compiler for Dual-Rail Qubits That Delays Gate Choices Until Routing
entry.summary: PRISM: A Logical-Physical Boundary Compiler for Dual-Rail Qubits arXiv · Nov 18, 2026PRISM is a compiler for dual-rail cavity qubits, which encode each logical qubit across multiple physical degrees of freedom to detect or correct errors. It keeps several equivalent realizations of each logical gate open and commits to one only when routing reaches a layout that can execute it. Across 25 workloads compared with a greedy search that fixes realizations before routing, it reports 20.4–30.8% fewer routing SWAPs and 8.8–10.1% lower physical depth.

entry.title: Variable-length MDI QKD with source imperfections and horizontal-link randomization
entry.summary: Variable-length MDI QKD under source imperfections and local randomization over horizontal links arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies the security of measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) when the sources of Alice and Bob are imperfect and block sizes are finite. The authors model source imperfections using fidelity bounds and establish variable-length general security under the Marginal-constrained Entropy Accumulation Theorem, estimating Rényi entropies via conic optimization. They report secret keys for blocks as small as about 3x10^4 rounds over an atmosphere-free horizontal channel, and show that choosing transmitted amplitudes to compensate unequal attenuation improves performance in asymmetric setups.

entry.title: Dynamical decoupling using continuous unitary designs to protect qubit coherence
entry.summary: Dynamical Decoupling via Continuous Unitary Design arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes a dynamical decoupling framework based on continuous unitary designs that suppresses arbitrary static noise during continuous control. The authors derive closed-form phase conditions for suppressing Rabi-amplitude errors and unify universal decoupling, finite-pulse compatibility, and control-error robustness in one analytical framework. Experiments on a superconducting quantum cloud platform show significantly extended coherence times and the highest robustness to Rabi-amplitude errors and detuning among the tested sequences.

entry.title: Non-invertible quantum cellular automata I: a microscopic definition of non-invertible symmetries
entry.summary: Non-Invertible Quantum Cellular Automata I: Microscopic Definition of Non-Invertible Symmetries arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper introduces non-invertible quantum cellular automata (QCAs), defined as locality-preserving, dualizable, pure quantum channels, giving an operator-algebraic definition of non-invertible symmetries in quantum lattice systems based on their action on local operators. Focusing on quantum spin chains, the authors motivate these conditions and conjecture that every such channel can be realized by dualizable topological defects or dualizable sequential quantum circuits. They construct a broad class of examples, including anomalous on-site non-invertible symmetries and higher-dimensional cases.

entry.title: Problem-adjusted X-mixer eigenstates to improve QAOA performance
entry.summary: Problem-adjusted X-mixer eigenstates for improved QAOA arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies using problem-adjusted excited eigenstates of the X-mixer Hamiltonian as initial states for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on problems with degenerate ground states. The authors report that this advantage persists under quantum gate and readout noise, outperforming standard ground-state initialization, with the benefit depending on the number of QAOA layers and the initial state's evolution path into the problem's ground space. The paper also describes how to prepare these eigenstates exactly or approximate them with linear combinations of ladder operators.

entry.title: A Method for More Accurate Modeling of Particles Trapped in Magnetic Fields
entry.summary: Development of a Discrete Variable Representation of a Field-Adaptive Hermite Basis for Accurate Modeling of Magnetically Confined Systems arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper develops a magnetic-field-dependent Hermite-function discrete variable representation (Hermite-B DVR) that adapts to magnetic confinement. It efficiently represents wavefunctions across a wide range of field strengths using fewer basis functions. The method is benchmarked on two-dimensional quantum dots in perpendicular magnetic fields, showing excellent agreement with analytical spectra and wavefunctions. It is also applied to arbitrary confinement potentials and tilted fields.

entry.title: Exact classical bounds for bipartite Bell inequalities via improved branch-and-bound
entry.summary: Exact classical bounds of bipartite correlation Bell inequalities using improved branch-and-bound arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents an improved branch-and-bound algorithm for computing the exact classical (local) bounds of bipartite correlation Bell inequalities. It uses a see-saw-based heuristic to obtain a strong initial lower bound and greedy row reordering to tighten pruning, with an OpenMP parallel implementation. Benchmarks show large runtime reductions on random matrices, and exact computations are reported for square matrices up to 130×130 and rectangular matrices up to 81×321. Applications include improved lower bounds on finite-order Grothendieck constants for d=3,4,5,7 and XOR games with quantum-to-classical ratios exceeding √2.

entry.title: Computing molecular energies on a trapped-ion quantum computer with sparse quantum prolate diagonalization
entry.summary: Molecular energies from sparse quantum prolate diagonalization on a trapped-ion quantum processor arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper introduces sparse quantum prolate diagonalization, which combines QPD with compressed sensing to exploit the sparsity of molecular Hamiltonian spectra. Using a two-orbital embedded Hamiltonian for an arginine–tryptophan pair in water, the authors run the method on the Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion computer. They report chemical-accuracy energies with circuits of up to 448 two-qubit gates.

entry.title: Oblique incidence and non-commuting limits: notes on convergence of Fresnel integrals
entry.summary: Oblique incidence and non-commuting limits: a remark on the convergence of Fresnel integrals arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The Gaussian integrals in quantum mechanics and paraxial optics are oscillatory and only conditionally convergent. The paper shows the one-dimensional Fresnel integral converges on its own, while the two-dimensional result depends on the shape of the expanding domain: it converges over squares but oscillates forever over discs. It also notes that at oblique incidence the integral converges and normal incidence is recovered in the limit, and that these two limits do not commute.

entry.title: Depth-dependent collapse and warm-start limits of a symmetry-preserving VQE on the J1-J2 Heisenberg ring
entry.summary: Depth-Dependent Collapse and Warm-Start Limits of a Symmetry-Preserving VQE for the J₁--J₂ Heisenberg Ring arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies a symmetry-preserving variational quantum eigensolver ansatz of SingleExcitationMinus gates, started from the Néel state, applied to the frustrated spin-1/2 J1-J2 Heisenberg ring with 10 and 12 sites. With random initialization, fidelity and energy error change abruptly at intermediate circuit depth, showing improvement, degradation and recovery. A chained warm start that extends an optimized shallow circuit with identity layers removes the collapse, but for some frustration values fidelity stalls at about 0.50 to 0.58 despite small energy error, so low energy alone does not reach the ground state.

entry.title: How every physicist could accept Bohmian mechanics: a reformulation as a macroscopic description
entry.summary: How can every physicist become a Bohmian arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes reformulating Bohmian mechanics so that deterministic trajectories describe the macroscopic pointer of a measuring apparatus rather than microscopic particles. It makes no claims about the fundamental nature of the microscopic world. In this form, Bohmian trajectories serve as a practical tool for visualizing how a definite measurement outcome emerges, which the authors suggest makes the approach acceptable to physicists who would otherwise reject the Bohmian program.

entry.title: Time-travel paradox in a Bohmian extension of Deutsch's approach, where tunneling becomes mandatory
entry.summary: Time-Travel Paradox in a Bohmian Extension of Deutsch's Approach: Mandatory Tunneling as the "Banana Peel Mechanism" arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper studies a self-prevention paradox in which a particle travels through a wormhole into its own past and blocks its own motion. It extends Deutsch's quantum self-consistency approach within de Broglie-Bohm theory by also requiring the particle's ontic configuration to be self-consistent. In a two-channel, narrow-band Gaussian approximation, the authors find a self-consistent solution in which quantum tunneling is mandatory, which they call the "banana peel mechanism".

entry.title: A quantum-classical density functional method for how molecules' light spectra change in different solvents.
entry.summary: Quantum-classical dynamical density functional theory for solvation dynamics arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents a modeling framework for thermalization and non-equilibrium spectroscopy in overdamped polar solvents, extending dynamical density functional theory to couple a molecule's electronic states with a polar solvent. The method is applied to a two-level polar dye in chloroform, dichloromethane, and dimethyl sulfoxide. Absorption and time-resolved emission spectra are computed from dipole-dipole correlation functions. The calculated solvent spectral response is reported to agree well with experimental relaxation trends.

entry.title: Quantum algorithms for preparing several excited states at once
entry.summary: Double-Bracket Quantum Algorithms for Preparing Multiple Excited States arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper introduces DB-MEX, a double-bracket quantum algorithm for preparing multiple low-lying excited states of a Hamiltonian. It combines an ensemble approach with double-bracket flows, using one recursively compiled circuit to evolve several orthonormal states that stay orthonormal by construction. The number and weights of the states determine whether the algorithm targets the lowest eigenstates, the p-th excited state, or their span. The authors prove convergence to the target for almost all initial states.

entry.title: Finite-key security of BB84 with passive receivers, proved by reduction to active measurements
entry.summary: Finite-key security of BB84 with passive receivers via reduction to active measurements arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies BB84 quantum key distribution with passive receiver basis choice, where detection-basis distribution may depend on the incoming photon number. The authors prove a reduction theorem that expresses the passive protocol's secret-key-length formula through an existing active BB84 formula via simple substitutions. The result applies to key-length formulas derived by the Shor–Preskill, Koashi, and Renner approaches, avoiding a separate security proof for the passive case.

entry.title: Exact test for whether the J/ψΛ spin state in LHC Λb⁰ decays is separable
entry.summary: An exact separability criterion for the J/ψΛ spin state in Λ_b⁰→ J/ψ\,Λ decays at the LHC arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper derives an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the J/ψΛ pair produced in Λb⁰→J/ψ(→μ⁺μ⁻)Λ(→pπ⁻) decays at the LHC, accounting for the Λb⁰ polarization. It proposes a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement using the full five-dimensional angular analysis. In idealized pseudoexperiments, this test reaches 90% rejection power at both 3σ and 5σ with about half as many signal events as a negativity test and a test based on angular moments.

entry.title: Reconstructing Memory Effects in Gaussian Noise for Photonic Quantum Systems
entry.summary: Tomographic reconstruction of non-Markovian Gaussian noise in continuous-variable photonic systems arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes a tomography framework that reconstructs memory effects in continuous-variable photonic systems directly from time-resolved homodyne data. It estimates an effective time-local Gaussian generator, described by drift and diffusion matrices, using regularized maximum-likelihood estimation constrained by complete positivity. Non-Markovianity is diagnosed through temporary violations of local CP-divisibility at the generator level, and numerical benchmarks cover memory-dependent loss, nonstationary thermal excitation, and pseudomode-mediated memory.

entry.title: A review of quantum random number generators: principles, practical challenges, and mainstream implementations
entry.summary: Quantum Random Number Generators: principles, practical challenges and mainstream implementations arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper is a review of quantum random number generators (QRNGs). It examines randomness from classical and quantum perspectives and surveys the main discrete-variable and continuous-variable entropy sources. It also covers entropy estimation, randomness certification, extraction, enhancement, and statistical validation. The authors compare representative implementations by performance, architecture, and generation rate, and discuss deployment issues such as scalability, trust assumptions, hardware integration, and cryptographic adoption.

entry.title: Complex quasiprobabilities as measurable temporal interference
entry.summary: Complex quasiprobabilities as measurable temporal interference arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes that the imaginary part of an extended Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability captures interference between many-body echo amplitudes, revealing dynamical differences that out-of-time-order correlators cannot resolve at infinite temperature. It proves the imaginary part vanishes for all unitary evolutions when either measurement has two outcomes, while generic dynamics with at least three outcomes, such as spin-1 systems, yield nonreal values. The authors also present an algorithm to reconstruct the full quasiprobability from local probe covariances, and show in a spin-1 chain that the imaginary signal distinguishes a Hamiltonian H from -H.

entry.title: Quantum non-Gaussian states induced by resonance below the critical point
entry.summary: Resonance-induced quantum non-Gaussian states below criticality arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies the Quantum Rabi Model, a single qubit coupled to a harmonic oscillator. It proposes that weak periodic qubit modulation below the critical point, combined with an adiabatic ramp that follows the instantaneous Floquet state, can produce quantum non-Gaussian states. When the modulation period is near Poincaré-Birkhoff resonances, the Wigner function shows pronounced non-Gaussian features that are more robust against loss than the superradiant ground state.

entry.title: Steering Qubit States on the Bloch Sphere via Measurement on a Continuous-Variable Pointer
entry.summary: Measurement-Conditioned Bloch-Sphere State Steering with a Continuous-Variable Pointer arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how measuring the position of a continuous-variable pointer coupled to a qubit through a state-dependent displacement interaction can move the qubit's post-measurement state along a trajectory on the Bloch sphere. The authors derive the conditional state, the outcome distribution, and the Bloch-sphere coordinates. A real Gaussian pointer yields a meridian trajectory, while a phase-engineered pointer yields a measurement-dependent azimuthal angle. The paper also discusses outcome-dependent unitary feedback for preparing a target state and distinguishes this from implementing a universal deterministic single-qubit gate.

entry.title: Quantum speed limits from symmetries: a numerical method for minimal-time bounds
entry.summary: Quantum speed limits from symmetries: A numerical analysis arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies target-specific quantum speed limits, which bound the minimal time needed to realize a given quantum operation. The authors propose a numerical procedure in which, for a given symmetry, the minimal symmetry-restoring perturbation is found by solving a semidefinite program, yielding the tightest achievable bound for that symmetry. The method is applied to a two-qubit CNOT gate, a SWAP on a spinless-particle chain, and Dicke state preparation on a qubit ring.

entry.title: Quantum differential interference contrast microscope: using quantum interference to improve phase sensing against environmental noise
entry.summary: Quantum differential interference contrast microscope arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper introduces a quantum version of differential interference contrast microscopy (qDIC) that uses quantum interference for polarization analysis. Compared with standard schemes using coherent light, it shows the approach can offer resilience to environmental disturbances such as acoustic vibrations, air currents, and temperature shifts. It aims to enhance phase sensitivity without sacrificing the simplicity and robustness of the optical setup.

entry.title: Whether five six-part orthogonal product states can be told apart using only local operations and classical communication
entry.summary: Local distinguishability of five six-partite orthogonal product states arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper studies whether a set of five six-partite orthogonal product states, where any two states are orthogonal on only one subsystem, can be distinguished using local operations and classical communication. The authors classify all feasible sets into five categories with 249 cases in total. They prove that all sets except two can be perfectly distinguished. The two exceptional cases are further discussed.

entry.title: Forecasting quantum Mpemba effects using quantum speed limits
entry.summary: Predicting Quantum Mpemba Effects from Quantum Speed Limits arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper asks whether anomalous quantum Mpemba effects can be anticipated before a system nears its stationary state. The authors use quantum speed limits as geometric indicators of the effect and benchmark them on dissipative qubits and open spin chains. They report that short-time speed limits can predict the effect at low cost and with reasonable precision across broad parameter regimes.

entry.title: Multilevel Effects and Limits of the Quantum Rabi Model in Ultrastrong Coupling
entry.summary: Multilevel Effects and the Limits of the Quantum Rabi Model in Ultrastrong Coupling system arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies the energy spectrum of a circuit in which a multilevel superconducting artificial atom is coupled to a resonator in the ultrastrong coupling regime. Using a circuit Hamiltonian, it analyzes how truncating higher atomic levels affects the low-energy spectrum. Based on Löwdin partitioning, the author evaluates the contributions of virtual transitions through higher levels and finds that diagonal energy corrections reduce two-level truncation errors over a wide parameter range. Readjusting effective Rabi parameters reproduces the multilevel spectrum only in some regimes, while systematic deviations remain in others.

entry.title: Quantum codes for spotting which qubit has a fault
entry.summary: Quantum Codes for Distributed Quantum Fault Sensing arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper studies how entangled probes spread across a modular quantum processor can identify which component has a fault, without needing protected storage qubits. The authors derive a quantum-code criterion for optimal distributed sensing of one unknown local qubit channel. They report that with every qubit exposed, suitable code states improve on independent probes by 50%, while pairwise entanglement gives no gain.

entry.title: Optimal control of many-body states in an XXZ spin chain using one local magnetic field
entry.summary: Quantum Optimal Control of Many-Body States in an Antiferromagnetic XXZ Chain with a Single Local Magnetic Field arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This study examines an open-boundary antiferromagnetic XXZ spin chain driven only by a time-dependent magnetic field on a single terminal spin. Using Krotov's algorithm to optimize the control field, the authors assess whether multi-particle many-body states, including highly polarized GHZ-type states, can be prepared. They find that global spin-flip symmetry restricts reachable states and that population transfer proceeds stepwise through intermediate magnetization sectors. Combining frequency-tailored seed pulses with an extended time window yields GHZ state preparation fidelities exceeding 0.927.

entry.title: Quantum entanglement under restricted experimental settings
entry.summary: Entanglement in restricted experimental setups arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper defines two notions of separability relative to a given experiment, called inner and outer separability. It identifies exactly when each notion departs from ordinary separability. The authors show that outer separable states, entangled or not, admit local hidden variable models for every behaviour generated by the available measurements.

entry.title: A quantum battery that resists aging through squeezing
entry.summary: Anti-aging Squeezed Quantum Battery arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes a quantum battery built from a continuous-variable bosonic mode that is resistant to decoherence. Using squeezing as the quantum resource gives the battery higher energy capacity and ergotropy. The authors study non-Markovian decoherence and find the squeezing-enhanced performance persists as long as the total system of battery and environment has a bound state in its energy spectrum. This tolerance also holds at moderate finite temperatures.

entry.title: Analytical model of superradiant bursts in extended atomic ensembles
entry.summary: Analytical prediction of superradiant burst dynamics in extended atomic ensembles arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents an open-system quantum theory of forward superradiant bursts in extended two-level atomic ensembles, using coupled Heisenberg-Langevin and Maxwell propagation equations. Assuming spatially uniform population inversion, the authors derive an analytical expression for the absolute photon emission rate into the selected forward optical channel. For the sample parameters considered, the expression quantitatively reproduces spatially resolved stochastic simulations up to an optical depth of about 200. At higher optical depths, longitudinal inversion gradients limit the approximation.

entry.title: Creating Large Mechanical Quantum Superpositions Using Qubit-Mediated Interference
entry.summary: Generating Massive Mechanical Superpositions through Qubit-Mediated Interference arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes a way to demonstrate a quantum superposition of a massive mechanical resonator without requiring exact ground-state cooling. The scheme couples the resonator to a spin qubit through magnetic force, using three π/2 pulses spaced half a mechanical period apart to produce observable interference. The authors state the protocol suits resonance frequencies from 1 kHz to over 100 kHz and that interference remains visible above 10 phonons. They also note that low-frequency implementations could offer a route to testing objective collapse models.

entry.title: Nonlinear function regression using quantum ensemble learning
entry.summary: Nonlinear function regression using quantum ensemble learning arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper introduces two ensemble-learning algorithms, Bagging and AdaBoost, to improve accuracy on nonlinear regression problems using quantum devices. Bagging trains variational quantum regressors independently, while AdaBoost trains them sequentially and achieves significantly better prediction accuracy. The authors add systematic feature selection and a feature-to-qubit mapping based on repeated feature encoding, and test the approach on four benchmark functions of varying nonlinearity.

entry.title: Optimizing interference zeros for finite-pulse transmission in waveguide quantum electrodynamics
entry.summary: Optimizing interference zeros for finite-pulse transmission in waveguide quantum electrodynamics arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper studies two separated quantum emitters coupled to a common waveguide at several contact points, where interference between contact paths makes each emitter's coupling quadratic in frequency detuning. Separating each local double zero into two simple zeros can improve the transmission of a finite pulse. For a lossless Gaussian pulse, the minimum error is two-fifths of that for coincident zeros. The optimal separation depends on the pulse spectrum and on the weights of reflection, absorption, and distortion, and the mechanism is realized in uniform and Su-Schrieffer-Heeger waveguides.

entry.title: Pulse optimization method for multi-time correlations in quantum control
entry.summary: Gradient Ascent Pulse Engineering for Multi-Time Correlations arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper introduces QRT-GRAPE, which combines the quantum regression theorem with gradient ascent pulse engineering to derive analytic gradients for objectives defined by multi-time correlations. It is applied to heralded remote entanglement generation between two nonidentical atom-cavity systems, examining the trade-off between photon-emission probability and conditional Bell-state fidelity. Starting from a flat-top Rabi pulse pair, the method raises the photon-emission probability product from 0.2802 to 0.3216 and the conditional Bell-state fidelity from 0.9356 to 0.9441.

entry.title: Optical magnetization in intrinsic graphene from quantum interband coherence
entry.summary: Quantum Interband-Coherence-Driven Inverse Faraday Effect in Intrinsic Graphene arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents an analytical quantum theory of the inverse Faraday effect, which converts the angular momentum of circularly polarized light into quasistatic magnetization, in intrinsic graphene. The authors show that the helicity-dependent orbital magnetization comes from an off-diagonal zero-harmonic component of the second-order density matrix rather than from carrier circulation or population imbalance. They derive closed expressions for the induced temporal surface magnetization, its finite-pulse dynamics, and the nonlocal stray magnetic field of the two-dimensional source.

entry.title: Quantum circuit compiler in the quspect SDK that picks routing options after resynthesis
entry.summary: Circuit compilation in the quspect quantum SDK: selecting routings after coupling-constrained resynthesis arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper describes and evaluates the circuit compiler in quspect, an open-source quantum computing SDK. At its highest optimization level, it screens routing candidates and ranks them by cost after coupling-constrained resynthesis. On 55 circuits across five topologies, it uses 0.616 times as many two-qubit gates as Qiskit O3 and 0.592 times its depth.

entry.title: Predicting logical errors and choosing geometries for rectangular surface codes under biased circuit-level noise
entry.summary: Logical error prediction and geometry selection for rectangular surface codes under biased circuit-level noise arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies unrotated rectangular surface codes under standard depolarizing and superconducting-inspired circuit-level noise models. The authors build geometry-dependent logical error rate models from unbiased simulations and use logical sensitivities to compare responses to localized idle bias and global physical error perturbations. Geometries chosen by the model are checked with direct biased circuit-level simulations, and at a physical error rate of 0.004 and target logical error rate of 10^-3, the rectangular codes reduce physical qubit overhead by up to 42.4% and 26.2% relative to unrotated square codes.

entry.title: CHEQ: An FPGA platform for testing quantum error correction decoders with fast noise sampling
entry.summary: CHEQ: A Concurrent Hardware Evaluation Platform for QEC Decoders via Batch-Invariant Circuit-Level Noise Sampling arXiv · Nov 17, 2026CHEQ is an FPGA platform for validating hardware quantum error correction decoders before deployment, combining on-chip noise sampling, concurrent decoder evaluation, scoring, and RISC-V control. Its Sampling Units use geometric skipping to draw error firing locations from circuit-level noise models, and the shot distribution is shown to be invariant to batch size under exact geometric sampling. On an AMD VCU118 FPGA at code distance 7 and physical error rate 10^-3, two Sampling Units supply 20 Helios decoders at 49.2 million shots per second, completing 10^10 shots in 3.4 minutes.

entry.title: Lasting and Temporary Maximal Entanglement Between an Atom and a Cavity Field
entry.summary: Emergence and Persistence of Maximal Atom-Field Entanglement in the Jaynes-Cummings model arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how maximal entanglement between a two-level atom and a single-mode quantized field in a cavity arises and persists under the Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian. Using von Neumann entropy as the entanglement measure, the authors show maximal entanglement occurs when atomic population inversion and the l1-norm of atomic coherence both vanish. The initial field state determines whether this entanglement persists or is only transient.

entry.title: Symmetry-selected entanglement loss at Floquet resonances in coupled qubits
entry.summary: Symmetry-selected entanglement death at Floquet resonances of parametrically coupled qubits arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies two identical, strongly coupled qubits whose coupling is modulated periodically in an anharmonic way, with each qubit damped by its own reservoir. At Floquet resonances selected by symmetry, the steady-state entanglement vanishes, while it stays close to its undriven value elsewhere. The authors also compare different master equations and show how the choice of basis and the secular approximation affect the entanglement.

entry.title: Pseudospectra of a relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
entry.summary: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies the resolvent norm of a relativistic non-self-adjoint operator obtained from the quantum harmonic oscillator through a dilation analytic transformation. The authors establish an upper bound for this norm. The bound shows that the norm decays for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than the dilation angle. This answers a question left open in a 2025 Proceedings of the Royal Society A paper.

entry.title: Simulating fluid flows on early fault-tolerant quantum computers while keeping nonlinearity
entry.summary: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how to simulate the evolution of a probability density for nonlinear dynamics on early fault-tolerant quantum computers. It combines polynomial reduced-order models fitted by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics with Walsh-synthesized Koopman-von Neumann transport and surface-code resource estimation. For a cylinder wake, the authors estimate 1.62 hours on about 560,000 physical qubits to reach 1% relative root-mean-square field error, and report nonlinear radial transport experiments on IBM hardware.

entry.title: Deciding integer 2×3×3 tensor isomorphism with quantum algorithms
entry.summary: Integral Tensor Isomorphism via Cubic Rings and Lattice Methods arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper proves that isomorphism of integral 2×3×3 tensors under GL₂(Z)×GL₃(Z)×GL₃(Z) can be decided in bounded-error quantum polynomial time. For nonzero determinant forms, it reduces the problem to principality tests for compatible lattices, using Wood's parametrization by balanced modules and algorithms of Bley, Hofmann, and Johnston. When the determinant form vanishes identically, the problem reduces to an integral 2×2×2 core or a polynomial kernel vector case.

entry.title: Optimal sample complexity for estimating min-entropy with high probability
entry.summary: Optimal Min-Entropy Estimation with High Probability arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper determines how many samples are needed to estimate min-entropy, a measure of how unpredictable a randomness source is, with high probability. The sample complexity is Θ(d log(d/δ)/ε²) for classical distributions on d symbols and Θ((d²+d log(1/δ))/ε²) for quantum states on a d-dimensional Hilbert space. The authors provide short and simple proofs of these results.

entry.title: Quantum Regression Method for Filling Gaps in Ship Performance Data
entry.summary: A Quantum Support Vector Regression Framework for Missing Data Imputation in Ship Performance Data arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines quantum support vector regression (QSVR) for filling in missing values in ship performance data, estimating marine fuel consumption. Using real data from a Panamax bulk carrier, it compares classical support vector regression with QSVR models based on different quantum feature maps under varying levels of data availability. The ZZFeatureMap_1 model achieved the highest average R² of 0.991 and the lowest aggregate imputation errors.

entry.title: MASQ: a measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford quantum error correction circuits
entry.summary: MASQ: Measurement-Adaptive Sampling for Near-Clifford Quantum Error Correction Circuits arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents MASQ, an exact sampler for near-Clifford quantum error correction circuits, designed to estimate rare logical failures in fault-tolerant protocols. At each measurement boundary it materializes only the non-Clifford rotations relevant to that measurement, and stabilizer-assisted elimination removes rotations that cannot affect any future measurement. Across 19 QEC benchmarks, MASQ reduces peak active width by up to 40 virtual qubits and achieves up to 8,098-fold CPU throughput speedup over Clifft on multi-round circuits.

entry.title: Helium State Calculation in a CAS(2,2) Subspace Using Photonic Quantum Circuits
entry.summary: Helium States Inspired by Quantum Photonics Circuit arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper implements the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm on a four-mode Fock-state photonic system to compute ground and excited-state energies of the neutral helium atom in a CAS(2,2) active space. The electronic Hilbert space is encoded into a bosonic Fock representation and optimized with a continuous-variable circuit built from phase shifts, beam splitters, and cross-Kerr interactions. In noiseless simulations, the ground and excited states retain unit survival probability within the target subspace, and results are benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the CASCI Hamiltonian.

entry.title: Robust Quantum Memory in 3D: Thermal and Zero-Temperature Perturbative Stability (Part I)
entry.summary: Robust Passive Quantum Memory in Three Dimensions, Part I: Thermal and Zero-Temperature Perturbative Stability arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines whether a three-dimensional quantum many-body system can passively protect encoded quantum information, a question open since Kitaev's work on topological quantum computation. The authors present a slight variant of the Balasubramanian, Davydova, and Lin (BDL) family of stabilizer codes that remains stable along both boundary axes of the perturbation-temperature phase diagram as system size grows. Without perturbation, the code is thermally stable below a critical temperature. At zero temperature under arbitrary weak, superpolynomially decaying quantum perturbations, it maintains a uniform bulk spectral gap and a superpolynomially long memory lifetime. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report that a variant of the BDL self-correcting code keeps a uniform bulk gap and superpolynomially small ground-space splitting under weak perturbations, advancing 3D passive memory.

entry.title: QCap: A Physics-Corrected Graph Neural Network for Capacitance Matrices of Superconducting Device Layouts
entry.summary: QCap: a physics-corrected graph neural network for the capacitance matrix of any planar superconducting device layout arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents QCap, a model that predicts the capacitance matrix of arbitrary planar superconducting device layouts in seconds, whereas Ansys Q3D simulations take minutes to hours. The model starts from a coarse physics estimate given by a fast method-of-moments simulation and is trained to correct it, using a universal graph format that accepts layouts from any tool. On 4,009 held-out test designs, its median error against Q3D is 0.177%, and it stays below 1% on unseen component families. It computes a 9-qubit device in 12 seconds on a laptop and a 100-qubit, 781-conductor device in 3.4 minutes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a universal graph embedding and a method-of-moments prior corrected by a GNN, reporting accuracy on thousands of designs and 9- to 100-qubit devices.

entry.title: Exact dynamic scaling of quantum jump counts in continuously monitored many-body systems
entry.summary: Exact Dynamic Scaling of Quantum Jump Statistics in Monitored Many-Body Systems arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how the number of quantum jumps within a subsystem fluctuates in many-body systems under continuous monitoring. The authors find that these fluctuations follow a dynamic scaling law with a diffusive time scale and an anomalous super-Poissonian dependence on subsystem size. For free fermions, they derive an exact finite-size solution of the Liouvillian autocorrelation function to determine the scaling exponent and scaling function. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a new dynamic scaling of subsystem quantum jump number fluctuations, with exact finite-size solutions for free fermions and extension to interacting fermions.

entry.title: Quantum reference frames and how they affect locality and causality in quantum field theory
entry.summary: Quantum Reference Frames, Locality, and Microcausality in Quantum Field Theory arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper studies how quantum reference frames for translations on Minkowski space affect the local structure of quantum field theories. Because of the relativistic spectrum condition, such frames are not described by projection-valued measures and often fail the weaker norm-1 localisation condition. As a result, strict locality becomes almost locality, and microcausality holds only through commutators that decay rapidly with separation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show frame observables cannot be projection-valued under the spectrum condition, replacing strict locality and microcausality with approximate versions.

entry.title: AI Scientist Finds Robust Quantum Control Sequences
entry.summary: AI Scientist Discovered Robust Quantum Control arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper introduces QORA, a multi-agent AI framework that combines theoretical reasoning with automated experimental calibration and control to discover quantum control sequences in a closed loop. Applied to a dense ensemble of spin-1 nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, it found AID-ROD sequences that nearly double the measured spin coherence time compared with the human-designed DROID-C3PO sequence. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an AI framework discovering pulse sequences that nearly double spin coherence in spin-1 NV centers over DROID-C3PO, with a suppression hierarchy.

entry.title: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound for python's lunch decoding
entry.summary: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound on python's lunch decoding arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies the cost of decoding bulk information in holographic tensor networks, linked to the python's lunch conjecture about exponential post-selection costs. In a Haar random oracle model, the authors prove that recovering even one logical bit with constant average advantage requires Ω(2^{m/2}) queries. Combined with an amplitude amplification upper bound, the query complexity at constant decoding accuracy is Θ(2^{m/2}). The paper also comments on other admissible unitary ensembles. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a tight Ω(2^{m/2}) query lower bound for python's lunch decoding in a Haar random oracle model, matching an amplitude amplification upper bound.

entry.title: Quantum-classical separation in distribution transport via nonlocal games
entry.summary: Quantum-Classical Separation in Probability Distribution Transport via Nonlocal Games arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper asks whether local quantum dynamics can transport classical probability distributions in ways local classical dynamics cannot. The authors show that two classical distributions can be connected exactly and reversibly by a constant-depth local quantum circuit, while classical stochastic transport needs a substantially larger spatial range. The separation is demonstrated explicitly on a one-dimensional chain and generalized to graphs using a construction based on nonlocal games. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use nonlocal games to separate quantum from classical local transport, reporting constant-depth quantum circuits reversibly connecting classical distributions on a 1D chain.

entry.title: A qubit control method for superconducting digital signals, demonstrated experimentally
entry.summary: Demonstration of a Qubit Control Scheme Compatible with Superconducting Digital Signals arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a control scheme for single- and two-qubit gates on superconducting quantum processors. It uses guiding waveforms to generate bipolar high-speed pulse sequences on a common clock, aiming at single-flux-quantum (SFQ) control systems that need fewer analog microwave sources. Simulations reach 99.99% fidelity for 40 ns single-qubit gates and 99.9% for 100 ns CZ gates. Experiments using an arbitrary waveform generator achieve 99.94% average single-qubit gate fidelity and 99.63% fidelity for 120 ns CZ gates.

entry.title: Testing quantum cause-and-effect structures using spatiotemporal correlations
entry.summary: Quantum Causal Compatibility from Spatiotemporal Correlations arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper asks which quantum causal structures can explain observed spatiotemporal correlations when no intervention-complete description of the process is available. It builds three-qubit pseudo-density operators from experimentally accessible Pauli correlations and derives conditions for compatibility with chain, fork, and collider structures by relaxing complete positivity. A semidefinite-programming method tests physical realizability, and Choi negativity measures the minimum violation of complete positivity.

entry.title: Exceptional-point sensing that achieves quantum advantage
entry.summary: Exceptional-point Sensing with Quantum Advantage arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies exceptional-point sensors, which use singular non-Hermitian dynamics to amplify responses to weak perturbations. Earlier work showed that a gain-loss-balanced dimer coupled to independent, phase-insensitive reservoirs amplifies signal and reservoir noise equally, so no quantum advantage arises. The authors engineer non-Hermitian dynamics in particle-hole Nambu space using a single common reservoir, producing an enhanced response protected from extra noise. They demonstrate quantum-metrological advantage for weak-signal sensing and static-parameter estimation.

entry.title: Charging a Two-Qutrit Quantum Battery Through Ising and Anisotropic XZ Heisenberg Couplings (a quantum battery stores and releases energy using quantum systems)
entry.summary: Two-Qutrit Quantum Battery Charging through Ising Model and Anisotropic XZ Heisenberg Interactions arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes a two-qutrit quantum battery made of two spin-1 systems coupled to an external field through anisotropic Heisenberg interactions. From the Ising model, it derives an exact analytical expression for ergotropy in parallel charging, and finds that collective charging outperforms parallel charging. Increasing the collective exchange coupling speeds up ergotropy evolution and raises the maximum average power, while the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction mainly reduces these quantities. In the XZ model, the DM interaction is beneficial when combined with longitudinal anisotropy and a sufficiently strong exchange coupling.

entry.title: Relevance-based sparsification of measurements for variational quantum algorithms
entry.summary: Variational Relevance-Informed Sparsification of Term Measurements for Variational Quantum Algorithms arXiv · Nov 17, 2026Repeated measurements are a major bottleneck in variational quantum algorithms. The paper finds that contributions of qubit-wise commuting measurement groups to parameter-shift gradients concentrate in a subset of groups, and introduces a learned controller that predicts group relevance from Hamiltonian, circuit, and state features to select measurements via a tunable coverage threshold. Across 15 molecular VQE settings, it saves 49.6% of nominal gradient-measurement shots with a mean absolute energy gap of 5.67 mHa relative to full QWC measurement. The authors also test whether large language models can solve the same selection task without fine-tuning.

entry.title: Recovering lost correlation energy in quantum chemistry via stabilizer-guided perturbation theory
entry.summary: Perturbative Recovery of Stabilizer-Subspace Correlations for Quantum Computational Chemistry arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper introduces Stabilizer-Subspace Perturbation Theory (SSPT) to recover correlation contributions lost when stabilizer projection discards Hamiltonian couplings, using the Contextual Subspace VQE as a representative application. Pauli terms removed by the projection are treated as perturbations, with energies evaluated via an Epstein-Nesbet-type second-order correction or a resolvent-based formulation. Molecular benchmarks show substantially reduced projection-induced energy errors, with chemical precision reached using fewer contextual qubits in several cases.

entry.title: Commutator-guided repair for shallow quantum circuits and the limits of classical accessibility
entry.summary: Commutator-guided repair and classical-accessibility boundaries for shallow quantum circuits arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies shallow quantum circuits that can be optimized but still fail to reach the states selected by a Hamiltonian under fixed depth and evaluation budgets. The authors propose a repair method that builds a pool of local Pauli rotations from low-order Hamiltonian commutators and companion axes, then selects a compact completion layer before full reoptimization. In 189 paired six-qubit trials, unrepaired circuits achieved no strict successes, while the repair and control selectors achieved varying success counts. The results are framed as a tradeoff between trainability, arrival, and classical accessibility, not as quantum advantage.

entry.title: Electrostatic screening and nitrogen-vacancy charge states at boron-doped and nitrogen-doped diamond junctions
entry.summary: Electrostatic screening and nitrogen-vacancy charge states in boron-doped/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper uses self-consistent Poisson-Fermi calculations to study the equilibrium electrostatics of junctions between boron-doped and nitrogen-doped diamond, and how these electric fields affect the charge-state stability of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers. The authors find two distinct electrostatic length scales in the nitrogen-doped substrate: a near-interface region of ionized donors that dominates band bending and sets the NV0/- charge-state boundary, and a longer screening tail from weak donor ionization in the bulk. The NV- depletion depth depends strongly on nitrogen concentration and only moderately on boron doping.

entry.title: Analog-memory waveform generator for cryogenic qubit control, a low-power way to produce control pulses for quantum bits.
entry.summary: Analog-Memory-Based Waveform Generation for Qubit Control arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes an arbitrary waveform generator for cryogenic qubit control that uses analog memory, separating slow waveform programming from fast waveform generation. Waveform samples are stored as capacitor voltages and read out repeatedly through buffered switching networks, without high-speed digital-to-analog conversion. A cryogenic prototype at 14 K generated Gaussian waveforms at 40 Msps using a 50 ksps programming rate, with no measurable voltage decay over 2 s. A room-temperature prototype reached 160 Msps.

entry.title: Cantor Correlations II: Synchronicity and Bisynchronicity
entry.summary: Cantor correlations II. Synchronicity and bisynchronicity arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies synchronous and bisynchronous no-signalling correlations defined over Cantor topological spaces, using both continuous variable quantum information and operator algebra approaches. It shows that the universal C*-algebra for bisynchronous graded correlations coincides with a projective limit of free wreath products of quantum permutation groups. The authors also analyse non-local games on Cantor spaces and their perfect strategies, and give a quantum information interpretation of a quantum isomorphism of locally finite graphs.

entry.title: Coexisting orders and dipolar Luttinger liquids in a Z_N quantum torus chain
entry.summary: Coexisting orders and dipolar Luttinger liquids in ℤ_N quantum torus chain arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper maps the ground-state phase diagram of a one-dimensional Z_N quantum torus chain, which is linked to dipolar cluster and dipolar Ising chains through noninvertible dualities. Using tensor-network calculations, bosonization and perturbation theory, it identifies a C phase where X and Z long-range orders coexist, and dipolar Luttinger liquid phases that separate coexisting phases from single-order phases. In these liquids, gapless dipolar excitations coexist with long-range order.

entry.title: Preparing magic states on superconducting hardware with lattice-surgery escape
entry.summary: Magic state cultivation with lattice-surgery escape on superconducting hardware arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper implements two magic state cultivation variants on IBM's publicly available Nighthawk processor to prepare a magic state in a distance-5 code. One is a lattice-surgery escape, and the other is a grafting escape with a switch added to a matchable code. Both begin with fault-tolerant T-state cultivation on a color code and are decoded with matching-based decoders. The authors report lower logical error rates than previous experiments and high T-state fidelity for the lattice-surgery escape.

entry.title: Generalized Schrieffer-Wolff transformation: a general closed-form method for effective Hamiltonians
entry.summary: Generalized Schrieffer-Wolff transformation arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper introduces a dual Schrieffer-Wolff transformation for strongly coupled systems and a generalized version (gSWT) applicable to any Hermitian operator and block partition. The authors establish a geodesic principle for fixing the canonical gauge. They also derive an exact closed-form generator at every order, written as a finite nested-commutator sum that depends only on the active gap set. The framework is illustrated with the collective spin model and the transverse-field Ising model.

entry.title: Transient synchronization and entanglement via shared dissipation in circuit QED
entry.summary: Transient Synchronization and Entanglement through Shared Dissipation in Circuit QED arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes a superconducting circuit in which two resonators couple to a common lossy auxiliary mode through DC-biased SQUIDs, with collective damping and correlated noise tunable by flux biases. For detuned resonators, mean amplitudes lock to a common frequency above an exceptional point, while resonant modes show transient synchronization with an analytical synchronization time. For initially separable squeezed states, the same relaxation converts local squeezing into transient entanglement, measured by logarithmic negativity.

entry.title: Space-based quantum sensors for testing fundamental physics
entry.summary: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space arXiv · Nov 17, 2026These proceedings from an Aspen Center for Physics workshop examine how quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can probe physics beyond the Standard Model. They use the space environment's microgravity and long baselines. The paper summarizes the scientific case, current capabilities, and mission concepts for studying dark matter, testing general relativity, and detecting gravitational waves in bands inaccessible from the ground.

entry.title: Speeding up auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo using mixed-precision random propagators
entry.summary: Accelerating auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo with mixed-precision random propagators arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents an algorithm for propagating auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) wavefunctions in mixed precision, targeting NVIDIA Tensor Cores with the TF32 format. Each full-precision array is approximated by two TF32 terms, and each full-precision matrix product is computed from three TF32 products accumulated in full precision. On hydrogen chain benchmarks, mixed-precision propagation was consistently faster than double-precision GPU propagation, with the advantage growing as system size increased. Local-energy deviations remained small over the propagation windows considered.

entry.title: A photonic Maxwell's demon proposed as an energy source
entry.summary: Photonic Maxwells demon as an energy resource arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes a new way to realize Maxwell's demon for photons and explores using it as an energy resource. The design uses multilayer dielectric mirrors that transmit certain wavelengths and reflect longer ones, combined with a material that irreversibly converts photon wavelength. A three-dimensional box built from these one-way mirrors acts as a self-operating photonic demon that accumulates and stores blackbody radiation, with applications in solar thermal energy and solar thermophotovoltaics. In the ideal optical limit, radiation enters but cannot exit after conversion, enabling repeated photon recycling and potentially approaching the 93.3% Landsberg limit for solar energy conversion.

entry.title: Transferring quantum information through molecular light-matter networks using a new effective-Hamiltonian method
entry.summary: Quantum Information Transfer in Molecular Polaritonic Networks: A Van Vleck Effective-Hamiltonian Approach arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper introduces Projected-Block Van Vleck Perturbation Theory (PB-VVPT), a method for modeling how quantum information moves through networks of molecules coupled to an optical cavity and vibrations. The approach is benchmarked on a molecular wheel network for transfers between molecules and from a molecule to the cavity. It reproduces exact dynamics with prediction errors below 1% over most simulated times, at a computational cost more than two orders of magnitude lower.

entry.title: Simplifying models of noisy quantum error-correction on leaking qubits via Pauli twirling
entry.summary: Simplifying models of noisy stabilizer QEC on leakage qubits by Pauli twirling arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper extends existing models of stabilizer quantum error correction (QEC) cycles to cases where physical qubits suffer leakage. The authors develop a leakage-dephased Pauli twirling theory and show that a QEC cycle with leakage can be modeled as a classical Markov process over joint syndrome and leakage patterns. They also derive a transfer-matrix description of repeated QEC cycles and an exact expression for the success probability of a QEC memory experiment.

entry.title: Probing real-time decoding accuracy limits in trapped-ion quantum architectures
entry.summary: Probing the real-time decoding accuracy bounds in trapped ion architectures arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies real-time error-correction decoding for trapped-ion quantum computers, which have millisecond cycle times that leave spare classical processing time. It proposes a hybrid sliding-window scheme in which a lower-accuracy decoder handles most windows and a higher-accuracy decoder is used only for low-confidence windows. Simulations of bivariate bicycle codes under trapped-ion-informed noise show logical error rates reduced by up to 3-4 orders of magnitude relative to BP-LSD and 2-3 orders relative to Beamsearch.

entry.title: A geometric framework linking local and global symmetry in molecular aggregates
entry.summary: A Geometric Framework for Local-to-Global Symmetry: Global Constraints on Local Dynamics arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines how the symmetries of local structural units in molecular aggregates relate to the symmetry of the whole aggregate. The authors build a covariant local-to-global representation from framed local symmetry data and use Frobenius reciprocity with standard character tables to determine symmetry-enforced dynamical exclusions. The construction is formulated for arbitrary geometries modeled as homogeneous spaces of an ambient transformation group.

entry.title: Quantum Fisher information matrices for time-evolved bosonic Gaussian thermal states
entry.summary: Quantum Fisher information matrices for time-evolved bosonic Gaussian thermal states arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how to estimate parameters describing a Gaussian unitary time evolution applied to a bosonic Gaussian thermal state. The authors derive a formula for the α-z information matrix of such time-evolved states. They compute its entries for a two-mode Gaussian thermal state after a beam splitter operation, and also give a formula for the SLD operator of the parametrized family.

entry.title: Long-wavelength collective modes carrying entanglement in harmonic lattices
entry.summary: Infrared fluctuations and collective entanglement modes in harmonic lattices arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how infrared fluctuations and spatial separation affect vacuum entanglement between two finite regions in the relativistic harmonic chain and its Lifshitz generalizations. It finds that logarithmic negativity stays uniformly bounded as the mass approaches zero, while mutual information diverges, so infrared-enhanced correlations do not give unbounded distillable entanglement. Using local symplectic consolidation, the authors identify the collective canonical modes carrying the negativity and track how their spatial participation changes with separation.
